fact: The Caspian Sea is the world's largest inland body of water, also described as the world's largest lake and usually referred to as a full-fledged sea.

title: Mount Bazardüzü
fact: Highest point of Azerbaijan: 2,706 m above sea level. Mount Bazardüzü is a mountain peak in the Greater Caucasus range on the border between Azerbaijan and Russia (Dagestan).

title: Teide
fact: Highest point of Spain: 3,715 m above sea level. Teide or Mount Teide is an active stratovolcano on the Spanish island of Tenerife, part of the Canary Islands. Its summit (at 3,715 m (12,188 ft)) is the highest point in Spain and the highest of any island in the Atlantic Ocean.

title: Lake Victoria
fact: Lake, 68,100 km², 83 m deep. Lake Victoria is one of the African Great Lakes. With a surface area of approximately 59,947 km2 (23,146 sq mi), Lake Victoria is Africa's largest lake by area, the world's largest tropical lake…

title: Lake Tanganyika
fact: Lake Tanganyika is an African Great Lake. It is the world's second-largest freshwater lake by volume and the second deepest, in both cases after Lake Baikal in Siberia. It is the world's longest freshwater lake. It is also the 6th largest lake by area.

title: Gangkhar Puensum
fact: Highest point of Bhutan. Gangkhar Puensum is the highest mountain in Bhutan and the highest unclimbed mountain in the world, with an elevation of 7,570 metres (24,836 ft) and a prominence of 2,995 metres (9,826 ft).

title: Khan Tengri
fact: Highest point of Kazakhstan: 7,010 m above sea level. Khan Tengri is a mountain of the Tian Shan mountain range in Central Asia. It is on the China—Kyrgyzstan—Kazakhstan tripoint, east of lake Issyk Kul in Kyrgyzstan.

title: Mount Paektu
fact: Highest point of North Korea: 2,744 m above sea level. Mount Paektu or Mount Baekdu is an active stratovolcano on the Chinese–North Korean border. In China, it is known as Changbai Mountain.

title: Nanda Devi
fact: 7,816 m above sea level. Nanda Devi is the second-highest mountain in India, after Kangchenjunga, and the highest located entirely within the country as Kangchenjunga is on the border of India and Nepal.

title: Terich Mir
fact: Terich Mir, 7,708 meters (25,289 ft), is the highest mountain of the Hindu Kush range, the 33rd highest peak in the world and the highest mountain outside of the Himalayas–Karakoram range. It is located in the Chitral District of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.

title: Noshaq
fact: Highest point of Afghanistan. Noshaq,also called Noshakh or Nowshakh, is a 7,492 m (24,580 ft) high peak in the Hindu Kush mountain range lying on the border of Afghanistan and Pakistan.

title: Lake Superior
fact: Lake, 82,350 km², 406 m deep. Lake Superior is a lake in central North America. The northernmost, westernmost, and highest of the Great Lakes, Lake Superior straddles the Canada–United States border with the Canadian province of Ontario to the north and east and the U.S. states…

title: Ismoil Somoni Peak
fact: Highest point of Tajikistan: 7,495 m above sea level. Ismoil Somoni Peak is the highest mountain in Tajikistan, as well as the former Russian Empire and Soviet Union before Tajikistan's independence. The mountain is named after Ismail Samani, a ruler of the Samanid Empire.

title: Lake Ontario
fact: Lake, 18,529 km², 244 m deep. Lake Ontario is one of the five Great Lakes of North America. It is bounded on the north, west, and southwest by the Canadian province of Ontario, and on the south and east by the U.S. state of New York.

title: Wake Island
fact: Wake Island, also known as Wake Atoll (Chamorro: Islan Wake), is a coral atoll which is an unincorporated territory of the United States in the Micronesia subregion of the Pacific Ocean.

title: Mount Aragats
fact: Highest point of Armenia: 4,090 m above sea level. Mount Aragats is an isolated four-peaked volcano massif in Armenia. Its northern summit, at 4,090 m (13,420 ft) above sea level, is the highest point of the Lesser Caucasus and Armenia.

title: Lake Michigan
fact: Lake, 57,750 km², 281 m deep. Lake Michigan is one of the five Great Lakes of North America. It is the second-largest of the Great Lakes by volume (1,180 cu mi; 4,900 km3) and depth (923 ft; 281 m) after Lake Superior and the third-largest by surface area…

title: Lake Malawi
fact: Lake Malawi, also known as Lake Nyasa in Tanzania and Lago Niassa in Mozambique, is an African Great Lake and the southernmost lake in the East African Rift system, located between Malawi, Mozambique and Tanzania.

title: Lake Chad
fact: Lake Chad is an endorheic freshwater lake located at the junction of four countries: Nigeria, Niger, Chad, and Cameroon, in western and central Africa respectively, with a catchment area in excess of 1,000,000 km2 (390,000 sq mi).

title: Mount Hermon
fact: Highest point of Syria: 2,814 m above sea level. Mount Hermon is a mountain cluster constituting the southern end of the Anti-Lebanon Mountains.

title: Lake Erie
fact: Lake, 25,744 km², 65 m deep. Lake Erie ( EER-ee) is the fourth-largest lake by surface area of the five Great Lakes in North America and the eleventh-largest globally.

title: Lake Huron
fact: Lake Huron is one of the five Great Lakes of North America. It is shared on the north and east by the Canadian province of Ontario and on the south and west by the U.S. state of Michigan.

title: Grossglockner
fact: Highest point of Austria. The Großglockner, or just Glockner, is, at 3,798 metres above the Adriatic (12,461 ft), the highest mountain in Austria and highest mountain in the Alps east of the Brenner Pass.

title: Lake Ladoga
fact: Lake Ladoga is a freshwater lake located in the Republic of Karelia and Leningrad Oblast in northwestern Russia, in the vicinity of Saint Petersburg.

title: Lake Balaton
fact: Lake, 592 km², 13 m deep. Lake Balaton is a freshwater rift lake in the Transdanubian region of Hungary. It is the largest lake in Central Europe, and one of the region's foremost tourist destinations.

title: Negev
fact: The Negev or Naqab is the name for a desert and semidesert area in southern Israel. Today, it forms the bulk of the Southern District of Israel, whose largest city and administrative capital is Beersheba (pop. 223,587), in the north of the Negev.

title: Hoverla
fact: Highest point of Ukraine. Mount Hoverla, at 2,061 metres (6,762 ft), is the highest mountain in Ukraine and part of the Ukrainian Carpathians. The mountain is located in the Eastern Beskids, in the Chornohora region.

title: Lenin Peak
fact: 7,134 m above sea level. Lenin Peak or Ibn Sina (Avicenna) Peak is a mountain in the Trans-Alay Range of the Pamir Mountains, in the Gorno-Badakhshan and Osh regions on the Kyrgyzstan–Tajikistan border.

title: Sněžka
fact: Highest point of Czech Republic: 1,603 m above sea level. Sněžka or Śnieżka is a mountain on the border between the Czech Republic and Poland, the most prominent point of the Silesian Ridge in the Giant Mountains.

title: Karakum Desert
fact: The Karakum Desert, also spelt Qaraqum and Garagum, is the 12th largest desert in the world, located in Central Asia. The name refers to the shale-rich sand beneath the surface. It occupies about 70 percent, or roughly 350,000 km2 (140,000 sq mi), of Turkmenistan.

title: Mount Kailash
fact: 6,638 m above sea level. Mount Kailash is a mountain in Ngari Prefecture, Tibet Autonomous Region of China. It lies in the Gangdise Shan mountain range of the Transhimalaya, in the western part of the Tibetan Plateau.

title: Lake Balkhash
fact: Lake Balkhash, also known as Lake Balqash, is a lake in southeastern Kazakhstan. It is one of the largest lakes in Asia and the 15th largest in the world. It is located in the eastern part of Central Asia and sits in the Balkhash-Alakol Basin, an endorheic (closed) basin.

title: Kebnekaise
fact: Highest point of Sweden: 2,135 m above sea level. Kebnekaise is the highest mountain in Sweden. The Kebnekaise massif, which is part of the Scandinavian mountain range, has two main peaks.

title: Mount Apo
fact: Highest point of Philippines. Mount Apo is the highest mountain peak in the Philippines, with an elevation of 2,954 meters (9,692 ft) above sea level. A large solfataric, dormant stratovolcano, it is part of the Apo-Talomo Mountain Range of Mindanao island.

title: Lake Albert (Africa)
fact: Lake Albert, originally known as Lake Mwitanzige by the Banyoro, Nam Ovoyo Bonyo by the Alur, and temporarily as Lake Mobutu Sese Seko, is a lake located in Uganda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

title: Musala
fact: Highest point of Bulgaria. Musala is the highest peak in the Rila Mountains, as well as in Bulgaria and the entire Balkan Peninsula, standing at 2,925.42 metres (9,597.8 ft).

title: Shkhara
fact: Highest point of Georgia: 5,193 m above sea level. Shkhara is a mountain peak and the highest point in Georgia. It is located on the Georgia–Russia border, in Russia's Kabardino-Balkaria region on the northern side, and the Svaneti region of Georgia in the south.

title: Monte Titano
fact: Highest point of San Marino: 739 m above sea level. Monte Titano ("Mount Titan") or Monte Brugola is a mountain of the Apennines and the highest point in the country of San Marino.

title: Muztagh Ata
fact: Muztagh Ata (meaning 'Ice Mountain Father' in Turkic languages), formerly known as Mount Tagharma and Wi-tagh, is the second highest of the mountains which form the northern edge of the Tibetan Plateau, with an elevation of 7,546 m (24,757 ft).

title: Lake Onega
fact: Lake Onega is a lake in northwestern Russia, on the territory of the Republic of Karelia, Leningrad Oblast and Vologda Oblast. It belongs to the basin of the Baltic Sea, and is the second-largest lake in Europe after Lake Ladoga, slightly smaller than Lebanon.

title: Galdhøpiggen
fact: Highest point of Norway: 2,469 m above sea level. Galdhøpiggen is the highest mountain in Norway, Scandinavia, and Northern Europe. The 2,469-metre-tall (8,100 ft) mountain is located in Lom Municipality in Innlandet county, Norway.

title: Kongur Tagh
fact: 7,649 m above sea level. The Kongur Tagh (meaning 'Brown Mountain' in Turkic languages) is the highest peak in the Pamir Mountains, and also the highest mountain wholly within the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region, China.

title: Lake Kivu
fact: Lake, 2,700 km², 485 m deep. Lake Kivu is one of the African Great Lakes. It lies on the border between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda, and is in the Albertine Rift, the western branch of the East African Rift.

title: Lake Maggiore
fact: Lake Maggiore or Verbano is a large lake on the south side of the Alps divided between the Italian regions of Piedmont and Lombardy to the south, and the Swiss canton of Ticino to the north.

title: Rakaposhi
fact: 7,788 m above sea level. Rakaposhi also known as Dumani is a mountain within the Karakoram range in Gilgit-Baltistan in Pakistan. It is situated in the middle of the Nagar and Bagrote valleys.

title: Dufourspitze
fact: Highest point of Switzerland: 4,634 m above sea level. The Dufourspitze is the highest peak of Monte Rosa, an ice-covered mountain massif in the Alps.

title: Suur Munamägi
fact: Highest point of Estonia: 317 m above sea level. Suur Munamägi is the highest peak in Estonia (and the Baltic states), reaching 318 metres (1,043 ft) above sea level.

title: Death Valley
fact: Death Valley is a desert valley in Eastern California, United States, in the northern Mojave Desert, bordering the Great Basin Desert. The World Meteorological Organization lists Death Valley as the site of the hottest surface temperature recorded on Earth.

title: Loch Ness
fact: Lake, 56 km², 272 m deep. Loch Ness is a large freshwater loch in the Scottish Highlands. It takes its name from the River Ness, which flows from the northern end.

title: Vänern
fact: Vänern is the largest lake in Sweden, the largest lake in the European Union and the third-largest lake in Europe after Ladoga and Onega in Russia. It is located in the provinces of Västergötland, Dalsland, and Värmland in the southwest of the country.

title: Lake Nicaragua
fact: Lake Nicaragua or Cocibolca or Granada is a freshwater lake in Nicaragua. Of tectonic origin and with an area of 8,264 km2 (3,191 sq mi), it is the largest fresh water lake in Central America, the 19th largest lake in the world (by area) and the tenth largest in the Americas…

title: Kamet
fact: 7,756 m above sea level. Kamet is the second-highest mountain in the Garhwal region of Uttarakhand, India, after Nanda Devi. It is the 29th-highest mountain in the world. It lies in the Chamoli District of Uttarakhand.

title: Namcha Barwa
fact: 7,782 m above sea level. Namcha Barwa or Namchabarwa is a mountain peak lying in southeastern Tibet. The traditional definition of the Himalaya extending from the Indus River to the Brahmaputra would make it the eastern anchor of the entire mountain chain…

title: Banaba
fact: Highest point of Kiribati: 81 m above sea level. Banaba is an island of Kiribati in the Pacific Ocean. A solitary raised coral island west of the Gilbert Island Chain, it is the westernmost point of Kiribati, lying 185 miles (298 km) east of Nauru…

title: Nevado Sajama
fact: Highest point of Bolivia: 6,542 m above sea level. Nevado Sajama is an extinct volcano and the highest peak in Bolivia. The mountain is located in Sajama Province, in Oruro Department.

title: Great Victoria Desert
fact: The Great Victoria Desert is a sparsely populated desert ecoregion and interim Australian bioregion in Western Australia and South Australia.

title: Lake Tana
fact: Lake Tana is the largest lake in Ethiopia and a source of the Blue Nile. Located in Amhara Region in the north-western Ethiopian Highlands, the lake is approximately 84 kilometres (52 miles) long and 66 kilometres (41 miles) wide, with a maximum depth of 15 metres (49 feet)…

title: Saimaa
fact: Saimaa is a lake located in the Finnish Lakeland area in southeastern Finland. With a surface area of approximately 4,279 square kilometres (1,652 sq mi), it is the largest lake in Finland, and the fourth-largest natural freshwater lake in Europe.

title: Mount Korab
fact: Highest point of Albania: 2,764 m above sea level. Korab is the highest peak of the eponymous mountain range and the fourth-highest mountain located entirely in the Balkan Peninsula, standing at 2,764 metres (9,068 feet).

title: Lake Sevan
fact: Lake Sevan is the largest body of water in Armenia and the broader Caucasus region. It is one of the largest freshwater alpine lakes in Eurasia. The lake is situated in Gegharkunik Province, at an altitude of 1,900 m (6,234 ft) above sea level. It is fed by 28 rivers and streams.

title: Lake Edward
fact: Lake, 2,150 km², 117 m deep. Lake Edward (locally Rwitanzigye or Rweru) is one of the smaller African Great Lakes. It is located in the Albertine Rift, the western branch of the East African Rift, on the border between the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda…

title: Lake Winnipeg
fact: Lake Winnipeg is a 24,514-square-kilometre (9,465-square-mile) lake in North America, in the Canadian province of Manitoba. Its southern end is about 55 kilometres (34 miles) north of the namesake city, Winnipeg.

title: Carrauntoohil
fact: Highest point of Ireland: 1,039 m above sea level. Carrauntoohil, Carrauntoohill or Carrantuohill is the highest mountain in Ireland at 1,038.6 metres (3,407 feet 6 inches).

title: Arabian Desert
fact: The Arabian Desert is a vast desert wilderness in West Asia that occupies almost the entire Arabian Peninsula with an area of 2,330,000 square kilometers (900,000 sq mi). It stretches from Yemen to the Persian Gulf and Oman to Jordan and Iraq.

title: Great Bear Lake
fact: Great Bear Lake in the boreal forest of Canada is the largest lake entirely in Canada, the fourth-largest in North America, and the eighth-largest in the world.

title: Pico Bolívar
fact: Highest point of Venezuela. Pico Bolívar is the highest mountain in Venezuela, at 4,978 metres (16,332 ft). Located in Mérida State.

title: Kyzylkum Desert
fact: The Kyzylkum Desert is the 15th largest desert in the world. Its name means 'Red Sand' in Turkic languages. It is located in Central Asia, in the land between the confluent rivers Amu Darya and Syr Darya, a region historically known as Transoxania.

title: Lake Maracaibo
fact: Lake Maracaibo is located in northwestern Venezuela, between the states of Zulia, Trujillo, and Mérida.

title: Qinghai Lake
fact: Lake, 4,400 km², 21 m deep. Qinghai Lake is the largest lake in China. Located in the Qinghai Province, to which it gave its name, Qinghai Lake is classified as an alkaline endorheic salt lake.

title: Fansipan
fact: Highest point of Vietnam: 3,143 m above sea level. Fansipan is a mountain in Vietnam. Its height was originally measured at 3,143 metres (10,312 ft) in 1909, but this value was later adjusted to 3,147.3 metres (10,326 ft).

title: Halti
fact: Highest point of Finland: 1,361 m above sea level. Halti is a fell at the border between Norway and Finland. The peak (elevation 1,365 m (4,478 ft)) of the fell, called Ráisduottarháldi, is in Norway, on the border Nordreisa Municipality and Gáivuotna Municipality (Kåfjord)…

title: Kékes
fact: Highest point of Hungary. Kékes is Hungary's highest mountain, at 1,014 metres (3,327 ft) above sea level in the Mátra mountain range. It is Hungary's third most popular tourist attraction, after Lake Balaton and the Danube, and has a number of skiing pistes.

title: Pico do Fogo
fact: Highest point of Cape Verde: 2,829 m above sea level. Pico do Fogo is an active stratovolcano located on the island of Fogo, Cape Verde, rising to 2,829 metres (9,281 ft) above sea level. The main cone last erupted in 1680, causing mass emigration from the island.

title: Aldabra
fact: Aldabra, the world's second-largest coral atoll (the largest is Kiritimati), is located east of the continent of Africa.

title: Aletsch Glacier
fact: The Aletsch Glacier or Great Aletsch Glacier (Grosser Aletschgletscher) is the largest glacier in the Alps.

title: Alpamayo
fact: Alpamayo or Shuyturaju is one of the most conspicuous peaks in the Cordillera Blanca of the Peruvian Andes. Alpamayo Creek originates northwest of it. The Alpamayo lies next to the slightly higher Quitaraju.

title: Antelope Canyon
fact: Navajo Upper Antelope Canyon is a slot canyon in the American Southwest, on Navajo land east of Lechee, Arizona.

title: Aoraki / Mount Cook
fact: Aoraki / Mount Cook is the highest mountain in New Zealand. Its height, as of 2014, is listed as 3,724 metres (12,218 feet). It is situated in the Southern Alps, the mountain range that runs the length of the South Island.

title: Avenue of the Baobabs
fact: The Avenue of the Baobabs, or Alley of the Baobabs, is a prominent group of Grandidier's baobabs (Adansonia grandidieri) lining the unpaved Road No.8 between Morondava and Belon'i Tsiribihina in the Menabe region of western Madagascar.

title: Azure Window
fact: The Azure Window, also known as the Dwejra Window (Maltese: it-Tieqa tad-Dwejra), was a 28-metre-tall (92 ft) natural arch on the island of Gozo, located just off the shores of Malta.

title: Ball's Pyramid
fact: Ball's Pyramid is an uninhabited islet in the Pacific Ocean located 20 kilometres (12 mi; 11 nmi) southeast of Lord Howe Island, between Australia and New Zealand. The steep rocky basalt outcrop is the eroded plug of a shield volcano and caldera that formed 6.4 million years ago.

title: Ban Gioc–Detian Falls
fact: Bản Giốc – Detian Falls or Bản Giốc Falls is a collective name for two waterfalls on the Quây Sơn River that straddle the international border between China and Vietnam; more specifically located between the Karst hills of Daxin County, Guangxi and Trùng Khánh District…

title: Bastei
fact: The Bastei is a rock formation rising 194 metres (636 ft) above the Elbe River in the Elbe Sandstone Mountains of Germany. Reaching a height of 305 metres (1,001 ft) above sea level, the jagged rocks of the Bastei were formed by water erosion over one million years ago.

title: Bay of Kotor
fact: The Bay of Kotor, also known as the Gulf of Kotor or just as the Boka, is a winding bay of the Adriatic Sea in southwestern Montenegro and the region of Montenegro concentrated around the bay. It is also the southernmost part of the historical region of Dalmatia.

title: Belogradchik Rocks
fact: The Belogradchik Rocks are a group of strangely shaped sandstone and conglomerate rock formations located on the western slopes of the Balkan Mountains (Stara Planina) near the town of Belogradchik in northwest Bulgaria.

title: Benagil
fact: Benagil is a hamlet in Portugal, located in the civil parish of Lagoa and Carvoeiro, on the Atlantic coast of the municipality of Lagoa, in the Algarve region.

title: Blue Grotto (Capri)
fact: The Blue Grotto is a sea cave on the coast of the island of Capri, southern Italy. Sunlight shining through an underwater cavity is reflected back upward through the seawater below the cavern, giving the water a blue glow that illuminates the cavern.

title: Blue Grotto (Malta)
fact: The Blue Grotto refers to a number of sea caverns on the south east coast of Malta, a short distance from the fishing harbour limits of Wied iż-Żurrieq, Malta.

title: Bonneville Salt Flats
fact: The Bonneville Salt Flats are a densely packed salt pan in Tooele County in northwestern Utah, United States. A remnant of the Pleistocene Lake Bonneville, it is the largest of many salt flats west of the Great Salt Lake.

title: Bora Bora
fact: Bora Bora is a French island group in the Leeward Islands, comprising the western part of the Society Islands of French Polynesia, an overseas collectivity of the French Republic in the South Pacific. Bora Bora has a total land area of 30.55 km2 (12 sq mi).

title: Bryce Canyon National Park
fact: Bryce Canyon National Park is a national park of the United States located in southwestern Utah.

title: Bungle Bungle Range
fact: The Bungle Bungle Range is a major landform and the main feature of the Purnululu National Park, situated in the Kimberley region of Western Australia.

title: Camargue
fact: The Camargue is a coastal region in southern France located south of the city of Arles, between the Mediterranean Sea and the two arms of the Rhône river delta. The eastern arm is called the Grand Rhône; the western is the Petit Rhône.

title: Caño Cristales
fact: The Caño Cristales is a river located in the Serranía de la Macarena, an isolated mountain range in Meta Department, Colombia. It is a tributary of the Guayabero River, itself a part of the Orinoco basin. Caño Cristales was found in 1969 by a group of cattle farmers.

title: Cappadocia
fact: Cappadocia is a historical region in Central Anatolia region, Turkey. It is largely in the provinces of Nevşehir, Kayseri, Aksaray, Kırşehir, Sivas and Niğde. Today, the touristic Cappadocia Region is located in Nevşehir province.

title: Carlsbad Caverns National Park
fact: Carlsbad Caverns National Park is a national park of the United States in the Guadalupe Mountains of southeastern New Mexico. The primary attraction of the park is the show cave Carlsbad Cavern.

title: Cerro Rico
fact: Cerro Rico, also known as Cerro Potosí or Sumaq Urqu; is a mountain in the Andes near the Bolivian city of Potosí.

title: Cheddar Gorge
fact: Cheddar Gorge is a limestone gorge in the Mendip Hills, near the village of Cheddar, Somerset, England. The gorge is the site of the Cheddar show caves, where Great Britain's oldest complete human skeleton, Cheddar Man, estimated to be 9,000 years old, was found in 1903.

title: Chocolate Hills
fact: The Chocolate Hills are a geological formation in the Philippine province of Bohol. A minimum of 1,260 hills, and possibly over 1,776, spread over an area of more than 50 square kilometers (20 sq mi).

title: Cliffs of Moher
fact: The Cliffs of Moher are sea cliffs located at the southwestern edge of the Burren region in County Clare, Ireland. They run for about 14 kilometres (9 miles).

title: Colca Canyon
fact: The Colca Canyon is a canyon of the Colca River in southern Peru, located about 160 kilometres (99 mi) northwest of Arequipa. With a depth of about 3,270 metres (10,730 ft), it is one of the deepest canyons in the world. Its length is about 70 kilometres (43 mi).

title: Cotopaxi
fact: Cotopaxi is an active stratovolcano in the Andes Mountains, located in Cotopaxi National Park in Cotopaxi Province, about 50 km (31.1 mi) south of Quito, and 31 km (19 mi) northeast of the city of Latacunga, Ecuador.

title: Crater Lake National Park
fact: Crater Lake National Park is a national park of the United States located in southern Oregon. Established in 1902, Crater Lake is the fifth-oldest national park in the United States and the only national park in Oregon.

title: Danube Delta
fact: The Danube Delta is the second largest river delta in Europe, after the Volga Delta, and is the best preserved on the continent.

title: Deadvlei
fact: Deadvlei is a white clay pan located near the more famous salt pan of Sossusvlei, in a valley between the dunes in the Namib-Naukluft Park in Namibia. Also written DeadVlei or Dead Vlei, its name means "dead marsh". Its Afrikaans name is Dooie Vlei.

title: Dettifoss
fact: Dettifoss is a waterfall in Vatnajökull National Park in Northeast Iceland, and is reputed to be the second most powerful waterfall in Europe after the Rhine Falls.

title: Olney, Buckinghamshire
fact: 1773 — The hymn that becomes known as "Amazing Grace", previously titled "1 Chronicles 17:16–17, Faith's Review and Expectation", is first used to accompany a sermon led by John Newton in the town of Olney, Buckinghamshire, England.

title: Battle of Kunovica
fact: 1444 — Christian forces defeat the Turks in the battle of Kunovica.

title: Mystras
fact: 1449 — Constantine XI is crowned Byzantine Emperor at Mystras.

title: Cape Canaveral Launch Complex 36
fact: 1968 — Surveyor program: Surveyor 7, the last spacecraft in the Surveyor series, lifts off from Cape Canaveral Launch Complex 36A.

title: Throgs Neck Bridge
fact: 1961 — Throgs Neck Bridge over the East River, linking New York City's boroughs of The Bronx and Queens, opens to road traffic.

title: St Mary's Church, Reculver
fact: 1808 — John Rennie's scheme to defend St Mary's Church, Reculver, founded in 669, from coastal erosion is abandoned in favour of demolition, despite the church being an exemplar of Anglo-Saxon architecture and sculpture.

title: Chełmno extermination camp
fact: 1942 — The Holocaust: Nazi Germany begins deporting Jews from the Łódź Ghetto to Chełmno extermination camp.

title: Botany Bay
fact: 1788 — The first elements of the First Fleet carrying 736 convicts from Great Britain to Australia arrive at Botany Bay.

title: Wesley College, Melbourne
fact: 1866 — Wesley College is established in Melbourne, Australia.

title: Emley Moor transmitting station
fact: 1971 — The current Emley Moor transmitting station, the tallest free-standing structure in the United Kingdom, begins transmitting UHF broadcasts.

title: Chahar Cheragh Square
fact: 1946 — In Iran, Qazi Muhammad declares the independent people's Republic of Mahabad at Chahar Cheragh Square in the Kurdish city of Mahabad; he becomes the new president and Haji Baba Sheikh becomes the prime minister.

title: Battle of Spion Kop
fact: 1900 — Second Boer War: Boers stop a British attempt to break the Siege of Ladysmith in the Battle of Spion Kop.

title: Hollywood Athletic Club
fact: 1949 — The first Emmy Awards are presented in the United States; the venue is the Hollywood Athletic Club.

title: Hale Telescope
fact: 1949 — The Hale Telescope at Palomar Observatory sees first light under the direction of Edwin Hubble, becoming the largest aperture optical telescope (until BTA-6 is built in 1976).

title: Saint Kitts
fact: 1624 — Sir Thomas Warner founds the first British colony in the Caribbean, on the island of Saint Kitts.

title: Capture of Mexicali
fact: 1911 — Mexican Revolution: Mexicali is captured by the Mexican Liberal Party, igniting the Magonista rebellion of 1911.

title: Cirkus (Stockholm)
fact: 1959 — The first Melodifestivalen is held at Cirkus in Stockholm, Sweden.

title: Menai Suspension Bridge
fact: 1826 — The Menai Suspension Bridge, considered the world's first modern suspension bridge, connecting the Isle of Anglesey to the northwest coast of Wales, is opened.

title: Marquette Branch Prison
fact: 1954 — The Detroit Red Wings played in the first outdoor hockey game by any NHL team in an exhibition against the Marquette Branch Prison Pirates in Marquette, Michigan.

title: Centre Block
fact: 1916 — The Centre Block of the Parliament buildings in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada burns down with the loss of seven lives.

title: Salt Lake Valley
fact: 1846 — The first Mormon pioneers make their exodus from Nauvoo, Illinois, westward towards Salt Lake Valley.

title: Operation Veritable
fact: 1945 — World War II: British and Canadian forces commence Operation Veritable to occupy land between the Maas and Rhine rivers.

title: Chester Racecourse
fact: 1539 — The first recorded race is held on Chester Racecourse, known as the Roodee.

title: Battle of Amba Aradam
fact: 1936 — Second Italo-Abyssinian War: Italian troops launch the Battle of Amba Aradam against Ethiopian defenders.

title: Sikhote-Alin meteorite
fact: 1947 — The largest observed iron meteorite until that time creates an impact crater in Sikhote-Alin, in the Soviet Union.

title: Ely Cathedral
fact: 1322 — The central tower of Ely Cathedral falls on the night of 12th–13th.

title: Campo de' Fiori
fact: 1600 — On his way to be burned at the stake for heresy, at Campo de' Fiori in Rome, the philosopher Giordano Bruno has a wooden vise put on his tongue to prevent him continuing to speak.

title: Sardinia
fact: 1861 — With Italian unification almost complete, Victor Emmanuel II of Piedmont, Savoy and Sardinia assumes the title of King of Italy.

title: Brussels Airport
fact: 2013 — Armed robbers steal a haul of diamonds worth $50 million during a raid at Brussels Airport in Belgium.

title: Fort Stoddert
fact: 1807 — Former Vice President of the United States Aaron Burr is arrested for treason in Wakefield, Alabama, and confined to Fort Stoddert.

title: Yekatit 12
fact: 1937 — Yekatit 12: During a public ceremony at the Viceregal Palace (the former Imperial residence) in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, two Ethiopian nationalists of Eritrean origin attempt to kill viceroy Rodolfo Graziani with a number of grenades.

title: Matagorda Bay
fact: 1685 — René-Robert Cavelier establishes Fort St. Louis at Matagorda Bay thus forming the basis for France's claim to Texas.

title: Swaminarayan Temple, Ahmedabad
fact: 1822 — The first Swaminarayan temple in the world, Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Ahmedabad, is inaugurated.

title: Corsica
fact: 484 CE — King Huneric of the Vandals replaces Nicene bishops with Arian ones, and banishes some to Corsica.

title: Christiansborg Palace (1st)
fact: 1794 — The first Christiansborg Palace in Copenhagen burns down.

title: Waco siege
fact: 1993 — Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms (ATF) agents raid the Branch Davidian church in Waco, Texas with a warrant to arrest the group's leader David Koresh, starting a 51-day standoff.

title: 2001 Nisqually earthquake
fact: 2001 — The 2001 Nisqually earthquake, having a moment magnitude of 6.8, with epicenter in southern Puget Sound, damages the Seattle metropolitan area.

title: Kronstadt rebellion
fact: 1921 — Following mass protests in Petrograd demanding greater freedom in the RSFSR, the Kronstadt rebellion begins, with sailors and citizens taking up arms against the Bolsheviks.

title: Great Slave Auction
fact: 1859 — The two-day Great Slave Auction, once thought to be the largest such auction in United States history, begins.

title: Castle Hill convict rebellion
fact: 1804 — Castle Hill Rebellion: Irish convicts rebel against British colonial authority in the Colony of New South Wales.

title: Suhrawardy Udyan
fact: 1971 — Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, political leader of then East Pakistan (present day-Bangladesh), delivers his historic 7th March speech in the Racecourse Field (Now Suhrawardy Udyan) in Dhaka.

title: Ryukyu Kingdom
fact: 1879 — Shō Tai formally abdicates his position of King of Ryūkyū, under orders from Tokyo, ending the Ryukyu Kingdom.

title: Elba
fact: 1815 — Participants at the Congress of Vienna declare Napoleon an outlaw following his escape from Elba.

title: Escondida
fact: 1991 — Escondida in Chile's Atacama Desert – which was to become the worlds most productive copper mine – is officially inaugurated.

title: Siege of Damascus (1400)
fact: 1400 — Turko-Mongol emperor Timur sacks Damascus.

title: Great New Orleans Fire (1788)
fact: 1788 — A fire in New Orleans leaves most of the town in ruins.

title: Wat Phra Kaew
fact: 1784 — The Emerald Buddha is moved with great ceremony to its current location in Wat Phra Kaew, Thailand.

title: Crete
fact: 1905 — Eleftherios Venizelos calls for Crete's union with Greece, and begins what is to be known as the Theriso revolt.

title: San Giacomo di Rialto
fact: 421 CE — Italian city Venice is founded with the dedication of the first church, that of San Giacomo di Rialto on the islet of Rialto.

title: Boukoleon Palace
fact: 919 CE — Romanos Lekapenos seizes the Boukoleon Palace in Constantinople and becomes regent of the Byzantine emperor Constantine VII.

title: New Britain
fact: 1700 — William Dampier is the first European to circumnavigate New Britain, discovering it is an island (which he names Nova Britannia) rather than part of New Guinea.

title: Athens International Airport
fact: 2001 — Athens International Airport Eleftherios Venizelos begins operation.

title: Taipei 101
fact: 2004 — The Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat certifies Taipei 101 as the world's tallest building, based on the building having been topped out on 1 July 2003, even though the building was not completed until 31 December 2004.

title: Sicily
fact: 1282 — The people of Sicily rebel against the Angevin king Charles I, in what becomes known as the Sicilian Vespers.

title: Cretan State
fact: 1900 — Prince George becomes absolute monarch of the Cretan State.

title: Jim Corbett National Park
fact: 1973 — Project Tiger, a tiger conservation project, is launched in the Jim Corbett National Park, India.

title: Stand in the Schoolhouse Door
fact: 1986 — Alabama governor George Wallace, a former segregationist, best known for the "Stand in the Schoolhouse Door", announces that he will not seek a fifth four-year term and will retire from public life upon the end of his term in January 1987.
story_label: Wikipedia: Stand in the Schoolhouse Door

title: Colonial Building
fact: 1932 — Dominion of Newfoundland: Ten thousand rioters seize the Colonial Building leading to the end of self-government.

title: Casa de la Vall
fact: 1933 — Andorran Revolution: The Young Andorrans occupy the Casa de la Vall and force the government to hold democratic elections with universal male suffrage.

title: St. Nicholas Church, Leipzig
fact: 1724 — Premiere performance of Bach's St John Passion, BWV 245, at St. Nicholas Church, Leipzig.

title: Theater an der Wien
fact: 1805 — German composer Ludwig van Beethoven premieres his Third Symphony, at the Theater an der Wien in Vienna.

title: RAF Fairford
fact: 1969 — The first British-built Concorde 002 makes its maiden flight from Filton to RAF Fairford with Brian Trubshaw as the test pilot.

title: St Mary Magdalene Church, Sandringham
fact: 1871 — Funeral of Prince Alexander John of Wales at St Mary Magdalene Church, Sandringham.
story_label: Wikipedia: St Mary Magdalene Church, Sandringham

title: Fort Ricasoli
fact: 1807 — The Froberg mutiny on Malta ends when the remaining mutineers blow up the magazine of Fort Ricasoli.

title: Stortorvet
fact: 1858 — The 1858 Christiania fire severely destroys several city blocks near Stortorvet in Christiania, Norway, and about 1,000 people lose their homes.

title: American School for the Deaf
fact: 1817 — Thomas Hopkins Gallaudet and Laurent Clerc found the American School for the Deaf (then called the Connecticut Asylum for the Education and Instruction of Deaf and Dumb Persons), the first American school for deaf students, in Hartford, Connecticut.
story_label: Wikipedia: American School for the Deaf

title: Lake Champlain
fact: 1818 — The United States Senate ratifies the Rush–Bagot Treaty, limiting naval armaments on the Great Lakes and Lake Champlain.

title: Natural Bridges National Monument
fact: 1908 — Natural Bridges National Monument is established in Utah.

title: Fremantle Prison
fact: 1876 — Catalpa rescue: The rescue of six Fenian prisoners from Fremantle Prison in Western Australia.

title: Ireland
fact: 1949 — The Republic of Ireland Act comes into force, declaring Éire to be a republic and severing Ireland's "association" with the Commonwealth of Nations.

title: Kishinev pogrom
fact: 1903 — The Kishinev pogrom in Kishinev (Bessarabia) begins, forcing tens of thousands of Jews to later seek refuge in Palestine and the Western world.

title: Archdiocese of Pisa
fact: 1092 — The Diocese of Pisa is elevated to the rank of metropolitan archdiocese by Pope Urban II.

title: San Diego–Coronado Bridge
fact: 1970 — Chicano residents in San Diego, California occupy a site under the Coronado Bridge, leading to the creation of Chicano Park.

title: Tsuruga Nuclear Power Plant
fact: 1981 — More than 100 workers are exposed to radiation during repairs of at the Tsuruga Nuclear Power Plant in Japan.

title: Mont Ventoux
fact: 1336 — Francesco Petrarca (Petrarch) ascends Mont Ventoux.

title: Church of Saint Sava
fact: 1595 — The relics of Saint Sava are incinerated in Belgrade on the Vračar plateau by Ottoman Grand Vizier Sinan Pasha; the site of the incineration is now the location of the Church of Saint Sava, one of the largest Orthodox churches in the world

title: Tahiti
fact: 1789 — The Mutiny on the Bounty occurs, with the ship's captain, Lieutenant William Bligh and 18 sailors, set adrift, and the rebel crew setting sail for Tahiti. Eventually the majority of rebels sail for Pitcairn Island.

title: Gran Canaria
fact: 1483 — Gran Canaria, the main island of the Canary Islands, is conquered by the Kingdom of Castile.

title: Niagara Falls State Park
fact: 1885 — Governor of New York David B. Hill signs legislation creating the Niagara Reservation, New York's first state park, ensuring that Niagara Falls will not be devoted solely to industrial and commercial use.

title: Haymarket affair
fact: 1886 — Rallies are held throughout the United States demanding the eight-hour work day, culminating in the Haymarket affair in Chicago, in commemoration of which May 1 is celebrated as International Workers' Day in many countries.

title: Rhodes
fact: 1481 — The largest of three earthquakes strikes the island of Rhodes and causes an estimated 30,000 casualties.

title: Benty Grange
fact: 1848 — The boar-crested Anglo-Saxon Benty Grange helmet is discovered in a barrow on the Benty Grange farm in Derbyshire.

title: Royal Albert Bridge
fact: 1859 — The Cornwall Railway opens across the Royal Albert Bridge linking Devon and Cornwall in England.

title: Dominican Monastery (Frankfurt)
fact: 1292 — Election of Count Adolf of Nassau as King of the Romans in the Dominican monastery of Frankfurt.

title: Battle of the Îles Saint-Marcouf
fact: 1798 — French Revolutionary Wars: A French force attempting to dislodge a small British garrison on the Îles Saint-Marcouf is repulsed with heavy losses.
story_label: Wikipedia: Battle of the Îles Saint-Marcouf

title: Newport, Rhode Island
fact: 1639 — William Coddington founds Newport, Rhode Island.

title: Battle of Djerba
fact: 1560 — The Ottoman naval forces inflict a defeat on a Spanish fleet in the battle of Djerba. This marks the highpoint of Ottoman naval dominance in the Mediterranean, which starts declining five years later after the failed siege of Malta.

title: Silverstone Circuit
fact: 1950 — The inaugural Formula One World Championship race takes place at Silverstone Circuit. The race was won by Giuseppe Farina, who would go on to become the inaugural champion that year.

title: Camp Dubois
fact: 1804 — William Clark and 42 men depart from Camp Dubois to join Meriwether Lewis at St Charles, Missouri, marking the beginning of the Lewis and Clark Expedition's historic journey up the Missouri River.

title: Nelson, New Zealand
fact: 1870 — The first game of rugby in New Zealand is played in Nelson between Nelson College and the Nelson Rugby Football Club.

title: Great Britain
fact: 1850 — The Arana–Southern Treaty is ratified, ending "the existing differences" between Great Britain and Argentina.

title: Church of Scotland
fact: 1843 — The Disruption in Edinburgh of the Free Church of Scotland from the Church of Scotland.

title: Rosenborg BK
fact: 1917 — The Norwegian football club Rosenborg BK is founded.

title: Schloss Weimar
fact: 1714 — Johann Sebastian Bach leads the first performance of his cantata for Pentecost, Erschallet, ihr Lieder, BWV 172, at the chapel of Schloss Weimar.

title: Manchester Ship Canal
fact: 1894 — The Manchester Ship Canal in the United Kingdom is officially opened by Queen Victoria, who later knights its designer Sir Edward Leader Williams.

title: Pedra Branca, Singapore
fact: 2008 — The International Court of Justice (ICJ) awards Middle Rocks to Malaysia and Pedra Branca (Pulau Batu Puteh) to Singapore, ending a 29-year territorial dispute between the two countries.

title: Uppsala Cathedral
fact: 1276 — Magnus Ladulås is crowned King of Sweden in Uppsala Cathedral.

title: Christ Church Cathedral, Dublin
fact: 1487 — The ten-year-old Lambert Simnel is crowned in Christ Church Cathedral, Dublin, Ireland, with the name of Edward VI in a bid to threaten King Henry VII's reign.

title: León Cathedral
fact: 1135 — Alfonso VII of León and Castile is crowned in León Cathedral as Imperator totius Hispaniae (Emperor of all of Spain).

title: Afsluitdijk
fact: 1932 — In the Netherlands, construction of the Afsluitdijk is completed and the Zuiderzee bay is converted to the freshwater IJsselmeer.

title: Tampa Bay
fact: 1539 — In Florida, Hernando de Soto lands at Tampa Bay with 600 soldiers with the goal of finding gold.

title: Diamond Rock
fact: 1805 — Napoleonic Wars: A Franco-Spanish fleet recaptures from the British the island of Diamond Rock, which guards the entrance to the bay leading to Fort-de-France, Martinique.

title: Baikonur
fact: 2003 — Europe launches its first voyage to another planet, Mars. The European Space Agency's Mars Express probe launches from the Baikonur space center in Kazakhstan.

title: Ixtoc I oil spill
fact: 1979 — A blowout at the Ixtoc I oil well in the southern Gulf of Mexico causes at least 3,000,000 barrels (480,000 m3) of oil to be spilled into the waters, the second-worst accidental oil spill ever recorded.

title: Raigad Fort
fact: 1674 — Shivaji is crowned as the first Chhatrapati of the Maratha Empire at Raigad Fort.

title: York Minster
fact: 1961 — Marriage of Prince Edward, Duke of Kent to Katharine Worsley at York Minster.

title: Siena Cathedral
fact: 1311 — Duccio's Maestà, a seminal artwork of the early Italian Renaissance, is unveiled and installed in Siena Cathedral in Siena, Italy.

title: Battle of Arklow
fact: 1798 — Irish Rebellion of 1798: Battles of Arklow and Saintfield.

title: Timor
fact: 1789 — Mutiny on the Bounty: HMS Bounty mutiny survivors including Captain William Bligh and 18 others reach Timor after a nearly 7,400 km (4,600 mi) journey in an open boat.

title: Vredefort impact structure
fact: Impact crater, 300 km across. The Vredefort impact structure is one of the largest impact structures on Earth. The crater, which has since been worn away, has been estimated at 170–300 kilometres (110–190 mi) across when it was formed…

title: Popigai impact structure
fact: Impact crater, 100 km across. The Popigai impact structure is the eroded remnant of an impact crater in northern Siberia, Russia. It is tied with the Acraman impact structure as the fourth largest verified impact structure on Earth.

title: Wilkes Land crater
fact: Impact crater, 500 km across. Wilkes Land crater is a hypothesized giant impact structure beneath the East Antarctic Ice Sheet in Wilkes Land, East Antarctica.

title: Meteor Crater
fact: Impact crater, 1.2 km across. Meteor Crater, or Barringer Crater, is an impact crater about 37 mi (60 km) east of Flagstaff and 18 mi (29 km) west of Winslow in the desert of northern Arizona, United States.

title: Manicouagan Reservoir
fact: Impact crater, 85 km across. Manicouagan Reservoir is an annular lake in central Quebec, Canada, covering an area of 1,942 km2 (750 mi2). The lake island in its centre is known as René-Levasseur Island, and its highest point is Mount Babel.

title: Allende meteorite
fact: Meteorite, 2 tonnes, recorded 1969. The Allende meteorite is the largest carbonaceous chondrite ever found on Earth. The fireball was witnessed at 01:05 on February 8, 1969, falling over the Mexican state of Chihuahua.

title: Murchison meteorite
fact: Meteorite, 100 kg. The Murchison meteorite is a meteorite that fell in Australia in 1969 near Murchison, Victoria. It belongs to the carbonaceous chondrite class, a group of meteorites rich in organic compounds.

title: Campo del Cielo
fact: Meteorite, 50 tonnes, recorded 1576. Campo del Cielo ("Field of Heaven" or "Field of the Sky" in English) refers to a group of iron meteorites and the area in Argentina where they were found.

title: Charlevoix impact structure
fact: Impact crater, 54 km across. The Charlevoix impact structure is a large eroded meteorite impact structure in the Charlevoix region of Quebec, Canada. Only part of the impact structure is exposed at the surface, the rest lying beneath the Saint Lawrence River.

title: Chesapeake Bay impact crater
fact: Impact crater, 85 km across. The Chesapeake Bay impact crater is a buried impact crater, located beneath the mouth of the Chesapeake Bay, United States.

title: Tookoonooka impact structure
fact: Impact crater, 55 km across. Tookoonooka is a large meteorite impact structure (astrobleme) situated in South West Queensland, Australia. It lies deeply buried within Mesozoic sedimentary rocks of the Eromanga Basin and is not visible at the surface.

title: Logoisk crater
fact: Impact crater, 15 km across. Logoisk crater or Logoisk astrobleme is a meteorite impact crater in Belarus near the city of Lahoysk. It is 15 kilometers (9.3 mi) in diameter and is estimated to be 42.3 ± 1.1 million years old (Eocene). The crater is not exposed at the surface.

title: Kaali crater
fact: Impact crater, 110 m across. Kaali is a group of nine meteorite craters in the village of Kaali on the Estonian island of Saaremaa. The most recent estimates put its formation shortly after 1530–1450 BC (3237 ± 10 14C yr BP).

title: Boltysh crater
fact: Impact crater, 24 km across. The Boltysh crater or Bovtyshka crater is a buried impact crater in the Kirovohrad Oblast of Ukraine, near the village of Bovtyshka.

title: Haughton impact crater
fact: Impact crater, 24 km across. Haughton impact crater is located on Devon Island, Nunavut in far Northern Canada. It is about 23 km (14 mi) in diameter and was formed 31–32 million years ago during the Early Oligocene.

title: Sudbury Basin
fact: The Sudbury Basin, also known as Sudbury Structure or the Sudbury Nickel Irruptive, is a major geological structure in Ontario, Canada. It is among the oldest and largest known impact structures on Earth.

title: Mjølnir crater
fact: Impact crater, 40 km across. Mjølnir is a meteorite crater on the floor of Barents Sea off the coast of Norway. It is 40 km (25 mi) in diameter and the age is estimated to be 142.0 ± 2.6 million years (Early Cretaceous). The bolide was an estimated 2 km (1.2 mi) wide.

title: El Ali meteorite
fact: Meteorite, 15.2 tonnes. The El Ali meteorite or Ceel Cali, literally meaning, "Ali's Well," is a 15,150-kilogram (16.70-short-ton) meteorite that was known to the local population in Somalia for generations, but officially recognized as a meteorite only in 2020.

title: Araguainha crater
fact: Impact crater, 40 km across. The Araguainha crater or Araguainha dome is an impact crater on the border of Mato Grosso and Goiás states, Brazil, between the villages of Araguainha and Ponte Branca.

title: Sylacauga (meteorite)
fact: The Sylacauga meteorite fell on November 30, 1954, at 12:46 p.m. local time (18:46 UT) in Oak Grove, Alabama, near Sylacauga, in the United States. It is also commonly called the Hodges meteorite because a fragment of it struck Ann Elizabeth Fowler Hodges (1920–1972).

title: Wolfe Creek Crater
fact: Impact crater, 875 m across. Wolfe Creek Crater is a well-preserved meteorite impact crater (astrobleme) in Western Australia.

title: Aorounga crater
fact: Impact crater, 13 km across. Aorounga Crater is an impact crater in Chad. The exposed remnant of the crater is 12.6 km (7.8 mi) in diameter and its age is estimated to be less than 345 million years (Carboniferous or younger).

title: Montagnais crater
fact: Impact crater, 45 km across. Montagnais is a meteorite crater located on the continental shelf south of Nova Scotia, Canada. It measures 45 kilometres (28 mi) in diameter, and its age is estimated to be 50.50 ± 0.76 million years (Eocene).

title: Saint Martin impact structure
fact: Impact crater, 24 km across. Saint Martin is an impact structure in Manitoba, Canada. It is located in the northern part of the Rural Municipality of Grahamdale, northwest of Lake St. Martin.

title: Willamette Meteorite
fact: Meteorite recorded 1902. The Willamette Meteorite, officially named Willamette and originally known as Tomanowos by the Clackamas Chinook Native American tribe, is an iron-nickel meteorite found near Oregon City in the Willamette Valley of the U.S. state of Oregon.

title: Vichada Structure
fact: Impact crater, 50 km across. The Vichada Structure is a probable impact structure along the Vichada River in Colombia (Vichada Department), South America. It is most likely the largest impact structure in South America.

title: Neugrund crater
fact: Impact crater, 8 km across. Neugrund is a meteorite crater in Estonia. It is 8 km (5.0 mi) in diameter and was previously estimated to have been formed in the Ordovician around 470 Ma, with later research revealing a possible Cambrian origin (around 535 Ma).

title: Brahin (meteorite)
fact: Meteorite recorded 1807. Brahin is a meteorite pallasite found in 1810. This is the second meteorite ever found in Russia (nowadays Belarus). Sometimes it is also called Bragin.

title: Cape York meteorite
fact: Meteorite recorded 1894. The Cape York meteorite, also known as the Innaanganeq meteorite, is one of the largest known iron meteorites, classified as a medium octahedrite in chemical group IIIAB.

title: Gweni-Fada crater
fact: Impact crater, 14 km across. Gweni-Fada Crater is an impact crater in the Ennedi Plateau in Chad. The Gweni Fada structure was first noted on the map NE 34 X Fada of the IGN (National Geographic Institute France) and aerial photographs in the 1950s of IGN by Alain Beauvilain…

title: Mistastin crater
fact: Impact crater, 28 km across. Mistastin Crater is an impact crater in Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada, which contains the roughly circular Mistastin Lake. The lake is around 16 km (9.9 mi) in diameter, while the estimated diameter of the original crater is 28 km (17 mi).

title: Oasis Impact Structure
fact: Impact crater, 18 km across. Oasis Impact Structure is a deeply eroded impact structure that is located 80 km (50 mi) south of the BP Impact Structure in southwest Libya. The associated impact crater has been entirely destroyed by erosion.

title: Acraman impact structure
fact: Acraman impact structure is a deeply eroded impact crater in the Gawler Ranges of South Australia. Its location is marked by Lake Acraman, a circular ephemeral playa lake about 20 kilometres (12 mi) in diameter.

title: Pingualuit crater
fact: Impact crater, 3.4 km across. The Pingualuit Crater, formerly called the "Chubb Crater" and later the "New Quebec Crater", is a relatively young impact crater located on the Ungava Peninsula in the administrative region of Nord-du-Québec, in Quebec, Canada.

title: Shiva crater
fact: The Shiva crater is a proposed impact crater on the Indian continental shelf, located offshore to the west of Mumbai. Paleontologist Sankar Chatterjee and his colleagues proposed that the crater was formed around the Cretaceous–Paleogene boundary.

title: Ensisheim meteorite
fact: The Ensisheim meteorite is a stony meteorite that fell on November 7, 1492 in a wheat field outside the walled town of Ensisheim in then Alsace, Further Germany (now France). The meteorite can still be seen in Ensisheim's museum, the sixteenth-century Musée de la Régence.

title: Gibeon (meteorite)
fact: Meteorite recorded 1838. Gibeon is a meteorite that fell in prehistoric times in Namibia. It was named after the nearest town: Gibeon.

title: Kaidun meteorite
fact: Kaidun is a meteorite that fell on 3 December 1980 on a Soviet military base near what is now Al-Khuraybah in Hadhramaut, Yemen.

title: Gosses Bluff impact structure
fact: Impact crater, 5 km across. Gosses Bluff (or Gosse's Bluff) is thought to be the eroded remnant of an impact crater. Known as Tnorala to the Western Arrernte people of the surrounding region, it is located in the southern Northern Territory, near the centre of Australia…

title: Fukang meteorite
fact: The Fukang meteorite is a meteorite that was found in the mountains near Fukang, China in 2000. It is a pallasite—a type of stony–iron meteorite with olivine crystals. It is estimated to be 4.5 billion years old.

title: Eagle Butte crater
fact: Impact crater, 10 km across. Eagle Butte is an impact crater in Alberta, Canada, named for a rural area west of the Cypress Hills. It is 10 km in diameter and the age is estimated to be less than 65 million years (Paleocene or earlier). The crater is not exposed at the surface.

title: Mien (lake)
fact: Mien is a lake in southern Sweden, 12 km (7.5 mi) southwest of the town of Tingsryd. The lake lies within a meteorite crater. The eroded crater is marked by a 5.5 km (3.4 mi) diameter circular lake (Lake Mien).

title: Morokweng impact structure
fact: The Morokweng impact structure is an impact structure buried beneath the Kalahari Desert near the town of Morokweng in South Africa's North West province, close to the border with Botswana.

title: Wabar craters
fact: The Wabar craters are impact craters located in Saudi Arabia first brought to the attention of Western scholars by British Arabist, explorer, writer and Colonial Office intelligence officer St John Philby…

title: L'Aigle (meteorite)
fact: L'Aigle is a meteorite that fell on 26 April 1803 over L'Aigle, Lower Normandy, France, during a meteor shower. Before the event, meteorites were generally considered a superstition and were mistrusted by the scientific community.

title: Puchezh-Katunki crater
fact: Impact crater, 40 km across. Puchezh-Katunki is a meteor crater located in the Nizhny Novgorod Oblast of the Volga Federal District, Russia. It is 80 km (50 mi) in diameter.

title: Serra da Cangalha
fact: Impact crater, 13.7 km across. Serra da Cangalha is an impact crater in Tocantins, Brazil. The crater is between 12 and 13 kilometres (7.5 and 8.1 mi) in diameter, making it the second-largest known crater in Brazil.

title: Spider crater
fact: Impact crater, 13 km across. Spider is an impact structure, the deeply eroded remnant of a former impact crater, situated in the Kimberley region of northern Western Australia, 18 km east of the Mount Barnett Roadhouse on the Gibb River Road.

title: Ternovka crater
fact: Impact crater, 11 km across. Ternivsky crater or Ternovsky crater (*outmoded) is a meteorite crater named after the locality Terny in the northern outskirts (Ternivskyi District) of Kryvyi Rih and also Kryvyi Rih Raion in Ukraine.

title: Kamensk crater
fact: Kamensk crater is an impact crater located 10 to 15 kilometres (6.2 to 9.3 mi) to the north of Kamensk-Shakhtinsky town in Rostov Oblast, Russia. It is 25 km (16 mi) in diameter and the age is estimated to be 49.0 ± 0.2 million years old (Eocene).

title: Karla crater
fact: Karla Crater is a meteorite impact crater in Tatarstan, Russia. It is 10 km in diameter and the age is estimated to be 5 ± 1 million years old (probably Pliocene). The crater is exposed at the surface.

title: Boxhole crater
fact: Boxhole is a young impact crater located approximately 180 km (265 km by road) north-east of Alice Springs in the Northern Territory, Australia.

title: Carswell impact structure
fact: Carswell is an impact structure within the Athabasca Basin of the Canadian Shield in northern Saskatchewan, Canada. It is 39 kilometres (24 mi) in diameter and the age is estimated to be 115 ± 10 million years (Lower Cretaceous). The impact structure is exposed at the surface.

title: Steinheim crater
fact: The Steinheim crater is a meteorite crater in Steinheim am Albuch, Heidenheim County, Baden-Württemberg, Germany. The crater is located at the north-eastern end of the Swabian Alb, 40km west of the much larger (24-km-diameter) Nördlinger Ries crater.

title: Tin Bider crater
fact: Impact crater, 6 km across. Tin Bider Crater is an impact crater that sits in dry, rugged terrain in Algeria. The crater was formed in the last 70 million years, perhaps in the late Cretaceous or early Paleogene Period.

title: Presqu'île crater
fact: Impact crater, 20 km across. Presqu'île is a meteorite crater in the territory equivalent to a regional county municipality (TE) of Jamésie in the Nord-du-Québec region of Quebec, Canada, located about 3 kilometres (2 mi) south of the city of Chapais.

title: Beaverhead impact structure
fact: The Beaverhead impact structure is the second-largest impact structure within the U.S. It lies within the states of Idaho and Montana. Estimated at 60 kilometers (37 mi) in diameter, it is among the largest impact structures on Earth.

title: Gardnos crater
fact: Impact crater, 5 km across. Gardnos crater (Gardnos krateret) is a meteorite impact crater in Nesbyen municipality in Buskerud, Norway. It is located inside Meteorite Park (Meteorittparken) at Gardnos 10 kilometres (6.2 mi) north of the town of Nesbyen.

title: Kara crater
fact: Kara is a meteorite crater in the Yugorsky Peninsula, Nenetsia, Russia. Heavily eroded, it is presently 65 kilometres (40 mi) in diameter, though it is thought to be originally 120 kilometres (75 mi) before erosion.

title: Kärdla crater
fact: Kärdla is a meteorite crater near the town of Kärdla in Estonia. It is 4 kilometres (2.5 mi) in diameter and its age is estimated to be about 455 million years (Late Ordovician). The crater is not exposed at the surface.

title: Lumparn
fact: Lumparn is a large bay devoid of islands in the main island of Åland, Finland, bordered by Sund to the north, Lumparland to the east, Lemland to the south and Jomala to the west.

title: Shoemaker impact structure
fact: Shoemaker is an impact structure, the deeply eroded remnant of a former impact crater, situated in arid central Western Australia, about 100 kilometres (62 mi) north-northeast of Wiluna. It is named in honour of planetary geologist Eugene Shoemaker.

title: Veevers crater
fact: Veevers crater is an impact crater located on a flat desert plain between the Great Sandy and Gibson Deserts in the centre of the state of Western Australia. The site is very remote and difficult to visit.

title: Zhamanshin crater
fact: Zhamanshin is a meteorite crater in Kazakhstan. It is 14 kilometres (8.7 mi) in diameter and the age is estimated to be 900,000 ± 100,000 years (Pleistocene). The crater is exposed at the surface.

title: Amelia Creek crater
fact: Amelia Creek crater is an impact structure (or astrobleme), the eroded remnant of a former impact crater, located in the Davenport Range, Northern Territory, Australia.

title: Amguid crater
fact: Impact crater, 550 m across. Amguid is a meteorite crater located in the Central Sahara, Algeria. It is approximately 500 to 530 metres (1,640 to 1,740 ft) in diameter and approximately 65 meters deep.

title: Manson impact structure
fact: The Manson impact structure is an impact structure near the city of Manson, Iowa where an asteroid or comet nucleus struck the Earth during the Cretaceous Period, approximately 74 million years ago. It was one of the largest known impact events to have happened in North America.

title: Obolon' crater
fact: Obolon' crater is a 20 km (12 mi) diameter buried meteorite impact crater situated near the village of Obolon, about 200 km (120 mi) southeast of Kyiv in Poltava Oblast, Ukraine.

title: Söderfjärden
fact: Söderfjärden is a polder in Ostrobothnia, western Finland, 10 kilometres south of the town of Vaasa. The plain is in an impact crater dating back to more than 640 million years ago (Proterozoic, near the end of the Cryogenian).

title: Talemzane crater
fact: Impact crater, 1.8 km across. Talemzane or madena is an impact crater in Algeria, 40 km south-east of Hassi Delaa (a small city).

title: Woodleigh impact structure
fact: Woodleigh is a large meteorite impact structure (astrobleme) in Western Australia, centred on Woodleigh Station east of Shark Bay in the Gascoyne region.

title: Aarhus (meteorite)
fact: Meteorite, 720 g. Aarhus is an H chondrite meteorite that fell to earth on 2 October 1951 at 18:15 in Aarhus, Denmark. The meteor split just before the otherwise undramatic impact and two pieces were recovered. They are known as Aarhus I (at 300g) and Aarhus II (at 420g).

title: Hraschina meteorite
fact: Hraschina is the official name of an iron meteorite that fell in 1751 near the village of Hrašćina in Hrvatsko Zagorje, Croatia.

title: Muonionalusta
fact: Meteorite recorded 1906. The Muonionalusta meteorite is a meteorite classified as fine octahedrite, type IVA (Of) which impacted in northern Sweden, near the border to Finland, about one million years BCE.

title: Toluca (meteorite)
fact: Meteorite recorded 1776. Toluca is a group of iron meteorites found in Jiquipilco, Mexico near Toluca.

title: Hiawatha impact structure
fact: Impact crater, 31.1 km across. The Hiawatha impact structure is a probable impact structure discovered beneath the Hiawatha Glacier in northwest Greenland, from which it gets its name.

title: Chiyli crater
fact: Chiyli Crater is an impact crater in Aktobe, Kazakhstan. It is 5.5 kilometres (3.4 mi) in diameter and the age is estimated to be 46 ± 7 million years. The crater is exposed at the surface.

title: Ilyinets crater
fact: Ilyinets Ukrainian: Іллінецький кратер, romanized: Illnets'kyy krater is an impact crater in Ukraine (Vinnytsia Oblast). It is 8.5 kilometres (5.3 mi) in diameter and the age is estimated to be 378 ± 5 million years (Upper Devonian). The crater is not exposed at the surface.

title: Kursk crater
fact: Kursk is an impact crater located in Kursk Oblast of the Central Federal District, Russia. It is 6 km (3.7 mi) in diameter and the age is estimated to be 250 ± 80 million years old (Carboniferous to Early Jurassic). The crater is not exposed to the surface.

title: Logancha crater
fact: Logancha Crater is an impact crater in Krasnoyarsk, Russia. It is 20 km (12 mi) in diameter and the age is estimated to be 40 ± 20 million years old. The crater is not exposed at the surface.

title: Nadir crater
fact: Impact crater, 8.5 km across. Nadir Crater is a buried impact crater on the Guinea Plateau in the Atlantic Ocean, around 200 kilometres (125 miles) off the coast of Guinea-Bissau. The feature is named after the Nadir Seamount, located 100 km to the south.

title: Odessa Meteor Crater
fact: The Odessa Meteor Crater is a meteorite crater in the southwestern part of Ector County, southwest of the city of Odessa of West Texas, United States. It is accessible approximately 3 mi (5 km) south of Interstate 20 at Exit 108 (Moss Road).

title: Roter Kamm crater
fact: Impact crater, 2.5 km across. Roter Kamm is a meteorite crater, located in the Sperrgebiet, within the Namibian section of the Namib Desert, approximately 80 kilometres (50 mi) north of Oranjemund and 12 kilometres (7.5 mi) southwest of Aurus Mountain in the ǁKaras Region.

title: Peekskill meteorite
fact: The Peekskill meteorite is the object resulting from a well-documented meteorite event that occurred in October, 1992, in Peekskill, New York, United States.

title: Kelly West crater
fact: Kelly West is a deeply eroded impact crater situated in the central Northern Territory, Australia. It was discovered during Government geological mapping and first reported in 1973, the evidence for impact coming principally from an abundance of shatter cones at the site.

title: Macha crater
fact: Macha is a field of five meteorite craters located 685 kilometers (425 miles) west-southwest of Yakutsk in the Sakha Republic in Siberia, Russia, ranging from 60 to 300 m (200 to 980 ft) in diameter.

title: Monturaqui
fact: Monturaqui is an impact crater in Chile. It lies south of the Salar de Atacama and was formed 663,000 ± 90,000 years ago by the impact of an IAB meteorite. It is 350 m × 370 m (1,150 ft × 1,210 ft) wide and 34 m (112 ft) deep and contains a salt pan.

title: Ouarkziz crater
fact: Impact crater, 3.5 km across. Ouarkziz Crater is an impact crater in Tindouf, Algeria. It is 3.5 kilometers in diameter and the age is estimated to be less than 70 million years (Cretaceous or younger). The crater is exposed at the surface.

title: Vepriai crater
fact: Vepriai is the largest impact crater in Lithuania, named after the town of Vepriai located at its center. The crater is not exposed to the surface, having been eroded and covered by sedimentary rocks during the last glacial period.

title: Albareto (meteorite)
fact: Meteorite, 2 kg. Albareto is a meteorite which fell in July 1766 near the frazione Albareto, of Modena, Emilia-Romagna, Italy.

title: Chinga meteorite
fact: Meteorite recorded 1913. The Chinga meteorite is an iron meteorite. It is structurally an ataxite with very rare kamacite lamella. The meteoric iron is a part of the lamella taenite.

title: Eagle Station meteorite
fact: Meteorite recorded 1880. The Eagle Station meteorite is a pallasite and type specimen of the Eagle Station group. It was found in 1880 close to Eagle Station, Carroll County, Kentucky (United States). The first description was made by George F. Kunz in 1887.

title: Gao–Guenie meteorite
fact: Gao–Guenie is a H5 ordinary chondrite meteorite that fell on Burkina Faso, West Africa, on March 5, 1960. The fall was composed of many fragments and it is one of the largest observed meteorite showers in Africa to date.

title: Mbosi meteorite
fact: Meteorite recorded 1930. Mbozi is an ungrouped iron meteorite found in Tanzania. It is one of the world's largest meteorites, variously estimated as the fourth-largest to the eighth-largest, it is located near the city of Mbeya in Tanzania's southern highlands.

title: Sutter's Mill meteorite
fact: The Sutter's Mill meteorite is a carbonaceous chondrite which entered the Earth's atmosphere and broke up at about 07:51 Pacific Time on April 22, 2012, with fragments landing in the United States.

title: Yardymly (meteorite)
fact: The Yardymly meteorite is an iron meteorite that fell in Yardymli Rayon, Azerbaijan on November 24, 1959. The remains were discovered in the nearby village of Aroos. With five individual specimens, the total weight of the meteorite is estimated at 150.29 kilograms (331.3 lb).

title: Santa Fe impact structure
fact: Impact crater, 10 km across. The Santa Fe impact structure is an eroded remnant of a bolide impact crater in the Sangre de Cristo Mountains northeast of Santa Fe, New Mexico.

title: Aouelloul crater
fact: Impact crater, 390 m across. Aouelloul is an impact crater in Mauritania. It is located in the Akchar Desert, part of the Sahara Desert, approximately 50 kilometres (31 mi) southeast of Atar. The crater is exposed, 390 metres (1,280 ft) wide and roughly circular.

title: Beyenchime-Salaatin crater
fact: Beyenchime-Salaatin is an impact crater (astrobleme) in the Russian Far East. It is 8 kilometres (5.0 mi) in diameter and is estimated to be 40 ± 20 million years old (Eocene).

title: Kaluga crater
fact: Kaluga is an impact crater located in Kaluga Oblast of the Central Federal District, Russia. It is 15 kilometres (9.3 mi) in diameter and the age is estimated to be 380 ± 5 million years old (Upper Devonian).

title: Lawn Hill crater
fact: Lawn Hill ‘crater’ refers to an Ordovician impact structure, the eroded remnant of a former impact crater, situated approximately 220 km north-north-west of Mount Isa in northwestern Queensland, Australia. The site is marked by an 18 km diameter ring of dolomite hills.

title: Liverpool crater
fact: Liverpool is a meteorite impact crater situated in Arnhem Land within the Northern Territory, Australia. It was named after the nearby Liverpool River. Liverpool is remote and difficult to access. The crater has a raised, near-circular rim averaging about 1.6 km in diameter.

title: Rotmistrivka crater
fact: Rotmistrivka is an impact crater in Cherkasy Oblast, Ukraine, which is located near the village of Rotmistrivka. The crater is 2.7 kilometres (1.7 mi) in diameter, with an age estimated at 120 ± 10 million years (Lower Cretaceous).

title: Sobolev crater
fact: Impact crater, 53 m across. Sobolev (or Sobolevskiy, Sobolevskii) Crater is a meteorite crater in the Far Eastern Federal District of Russia. It is 53 metres (174 ft) in diameter and is estimated to be less than 1000 years old. The crater is exposed at the surface.

title: Steen River impact structure
fact: Steen River is an impact structure in Alberta, Canada. It is 25 km (16 mi) in diameter and the age is estimated to be 91 ± 7 million years (Late Cretaceous). The structure is not exposed at the surface.

title: Tabun-Khara-Obo crater
fact: Tabun-Khara-Obo is an impact crater in the Dornogovi Aimag (province) the south-east of Mongolia. The crater, which is exposed at the surface, is 1.3 km (0.81 mi) in diameter.

title: Tswaing crater
fact: Impact crater, 1.1 km across. Tswaing is an impact crater enclosed by a 1,946 ha nature reserve, situated in northern Gauteng province, South Africa.

title: Agen (meteorite)
fact: Meteorite, 30 kg. Agen is an H chondrite meteorite that fell to earth on September 5, 1814, in Aquitaine, France. It is an ordinary chondrite that belongs to the petrologic type 5, thus was assigned to the group H5.

title: Erg Chech 002
fact: Erg Chech 002 (EC 002) is an ancient andesite meteorite discovered in the Erg Chech region of the Sahara Desert in Algeria.

title: Å, Moskenes
fact: Å is a village in Moskenes Municipality in Nordland county, Norway. It is located about 2 kilometres (1.2 mi) southwest of the village of Sørvågen on the island of Moskenesøya, towards the southern end of the Lofoten archipelago.

title: Accident, Maryland
fact: Accident is a town in Garrett County, Maryland, United States. The population was 338 at the 2020 United States census. Accident has been noted for its unusual name. A resident of Accident is called an "Accidental".

title: Adak, Alaska
fact: Adak, formerly Adak Station, is a city located on Adak Island, in the Aleutians West Census Area, Alaska, United States. At the 2020 census, the population was 171, down from 326 in 2010. It is the westernmost municipality in the United States and the southernmost city in Alaska.

title: Adamstown, Pitcairn Islands
fact: Adamstown is the capital and only settlement of the Pitcairn Islands, the only British Overseas Territory that is located in the southern Pacific Ocean. As of 2023, Adamstown has a population of 35, which is the entire population of the Pitcairn Islands.

title: Aghdam
fact: Aghdam is a town and the nominal capital of the Aghdam District of Azerbaijan. Founded in the 18th century, it was granted city status in 1828 and grew considerably during the Soviet period.

title: Atlit Yam
fact: Atlit Yam is a submerged Pre Pottery Neolithic C (PPNC) archaeological site located 300–400 meters off the coast of Atlit, Israel.

title: Attu Island
fact: Attu is an island in the Near Islands (part of the Aleutian Islands chain). It is one of the westernmost points of the U.S. state of Alaska. The island became uninhabited in 2010, making it the largest uninhabited island that is part of the United States.

title: Baiae
fact: Baiae is an ancient Roman town situated on the northwest shore of the Gulf of Naples and now in the comune of Bacoli.

title: Balestrino
fact: Balestrino (Ligurian: Barestin or Balestrin) is a comune (municipality) in the Province of Savona in the Italian region Liguria, located about 70 kilometres (43 mi) southwest of Genoa and about 30 kilometres (19 mi) southwest of Savona.

title: Bannack, Montana
fact: Bannack is a ghost town in Beaverhead County, Montana, United States, located on Grasshopper Creek, approximately 11 miles (18 km) upstream from where Grasshopper Creek joins with the Beaverhead River south of Dillon.

title: Barentsburg
fact: Barentsburg is the second-largest settlement in Svalbard, Norway, with about 300 inhabitants (2025). A coal mining town, the settlement is now almost entirely made up of Russian nationals.

title: Bartolomé Island
fact: Bartolomé Island is an uninhabited 1.2 square kilometres (0.46 sq mi) volcanic islet located in Sullivan Bay, just east of Santiago Island, in the Galápagos Islands. just off the east coast of Santiago Island.

title: Bat Cave, North Carolina
fact: Bat Cave is an unincorporated community in Henderson County, North Carolina, United States and is part of the Asheville Metropolitan Statistical Area.

title: Batman, Turkey
fact: Batman is a city and capital of Batman District in Batman Province, Turkey. It lies on a plateau, 540 meters (1,772 feet) above sea level, near the confluence of the Batman River and the Tigris and had a population of 452,157 in 2021.

title: Beelitz
fact: Beelitz is a historic town in Potsdam-Mittelmark district, in Brandenburg, Germany. It is chiefly known for its cultivation of white asparagus (Beelitzer Spargel).

title: Belchite
fact: Belchite is a municipality and town in the province of Zaragoza, Spain, about 40 km southeast of Zaragoza. It is the capital of Campo de Belchite comarca (administrative region) and is located in a plain surrounded by low hills, the highest of which is Lobo.

title: Bodie, California
fact: Bodie ( BOH-dee) is a ghost town in the Bodie Hills east of the Sierra Nevada mountain range in Mono County, California, United States. It is about 75 miles (121 km) southeast of Lake Tahoe, and 12 mi (19 km) east-southeast of Bridgeport, at an elevation of 8,379 feet (2,554 m).

title: Boring, Oregon
fact: Boring is an unincorporated community and census-designated place (CDP) in Clackamas County, Oregon, United States.

title: Bouvet Island
fact: Bouvet Island is an uninhabited subantarctic volcanic island and dependency of Norway. A protected nature reserve situated in the South Atlantic Ocean at the southern end of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, it is the world's most remote island.

title: Buzludzha monument
fact: The Monument House of the Bulgarian Communist Party, also known as the Buzludzha Monument, was built on Buzludzha Peak in central Bulgaria by the Bulgarian communist government and inaugurated in 1981.

title: Cahaba, Alabama
fact: Cahaba, also spelled Cahawba, was the first permanent state capital of Alabama, United States, from 1820 to 1825. It was the county seat of Dallas County, Alabama until 1866. Located at the confluence of the Alabama and Cahaba rivers, the town endured regular seasonal flooding.

title: Caleta Tortel
fact: Caleta Tortel is a coastal village in Chile. It is the administrative center of the commune of Tortel and is located between the mouth of the Baker River the largest river in Chile and a small embayment of the Baker Channel.

title: Calico, California
fact: Calico is a ghost town and former mining town in San Bernardino County, California, United States.

title: Chicken, Alaska
fact: Chicken is a census-designated place in Southeast Fairbanks Census Area, Alaska. It is a community founded on gold mining, and is one of the few surviving gold rush towns in Alaska. The population was 12 at the time of the 2020 census, up from 7 in 2010.

title: Christmas Island
fact: Christmas Island, officially the Territory of Christmas Island, is an Australian external territory in the Indian Ocean comprising the island of the same name.

title: Clipperton Island
fact: Clipperton Island, also known as Clipperton Atoll and previously as Clipperton's Rock, is an 8.9 km2 (3.4 sq mi) uninhabited coral atoll in the eastern Pacific Ocean.

title: Cocos Island
fact: Cocos Island is a volcanic island in the Pacific Ocean administered by Costa Rica, approximately 550 km (342 mi; 297 nmi) southwest of the Costa Rican mainland. It constitutes the 11th of the 15 districts of Puntarenas Canton of the Province of Puntarenas.

title: Coiba
fact: Coiba is the largest island in Central America, with an area of 494 km2 (191 sq mi), off the Pacific coast of the Panamanian province of Veraguas. It is part of the Montijo District of that province.

title: Consonno
fact: Consonno is a ghost town and former village in the Olginate municipality of the province of Lecco, in Lombardy, northern Italy.

title: Craco
fact: Craco is a ghost town and comune in the southern Italian region of Basilicata, abandoned after the 1980 Irpinia earthquake. It is a tourist attraction and a popular filming location. In 2010, Craco was included in the watch list of the World Monuments Fund.

title: Crozet Islands
fact: The Crozet Islands are a sub-Antarctic archipelago of small islands in the southern Indian Ocean. They form one of the five administrative districts of the French Southern and Antarctic Lands.

title: Cut and Shoot, Texas
fact: Cut and Shoot is a city in eastern Montgomery County, Texas, United States, about 6 mi (9.7 km) east of Conroe and 40 mi (64 km) north of Houston. Until 2006, Cut and Shoot was considered and called a town.

title: Darwin Island
fact: Darwin Island is an isolated northern member of the Galápagos Islands in Ecuador, the uppermost extent of an extinct volcano. It has an area of 1 square kilometer (0.4 sq mi) and reaches 165 meters (541 ft) above sea level.

title: Deception Island
fact: Deception Island is in the South Shetland Islands close to the Antarctic Peninsula with a large and usually "safe" natural harbour, which is occasionally affected by the underlying active volcano.

title: Dhanushkodi
fact: Dhanushkodi is an abandoned town at the south-eastern tip of Pamban Island of the state of Tamil Nadu in India. It is south-east of Pamban and is about 24 kilometres (15 mi) west of Talaimannar in Sri Lanka.

title: Dikson (urban-type settlement)
fact: Dikson is a closed port town located in northern Russia and is one of the world's northernmost settlements. Dikson is an urban locality (an urban-type settlement) situated in Taymyrsky Dolgano-Nenetsky District of Krasnoyarsk Krai.

title: Ding Dong, Texas
fact: Ding Dong is an unincorporated community in Central Texas, United States. According to the Handbook of Texas, it had a population of 22 in 2000. It is located within the Killeen–Temple metropolitan area.

title: Dull, Perth and Kinross
