title: Charles Bridge
fact: Charles Bridge is a medieval stone arch bridge that crosses the Vltava river in Prague, Czech Republic. Its construction started in 1357 under the auspices of King Charles IV, and finished in the early 15th century.

title: Charyn Canyon
fact: Charyn Canyon, also known as the Sharyn Canyon is a canyon on the Charyn River in Kazakhstan. It is located about 200 km (120 mi) east of Almaty, close to the Kazakh–Chinese border. The canyon is roughly 154 km (96 mi) in length.

title: Château de Chambord
fact: The Château de Chambord in Chambord, Centre-Val de Loire, France, is one of the most recognisable châteaux in the world because of its very distinctive French Renaissance architecture, which blends traditional French medieval forms with classical Renaissance structures.

title: Christ of the Abyss
fact: Christ of the Abyss is a submerged bronze statue of Jesus Christ by Guido Galletti, the original cast of which is located in the Mediterranean Sea, off San Fruttuoso, between Camogli and Portofino on the Italian Riviera.

title: Christ the Redeemer (statue)
fact: Christ the Redeemer is an Art Deco statue of Jesus in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, created by French-Polish sculptor Paul Landowski and built by Brazilian engineer Heitor da Silva Costa…

title: Cologne Cathedral
fact: Cologne Cathedral is a Catholic cathedral in Cologne, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It is the seat of the Archbishop of Cologne and of the administration of the Archdiocese of Cologne.

title: Coral Castle
fact: Coral Castle is an oolite limestone structure created by the Latvian-American eccentric Edward Leedskalnin (1887–1951).

title: Corn Palace
fact: The Corn Palace, commonly advertised as The World's Only Corn Palace and the Mitchell Corn Palace, is a multi-purpose arena/facility located in Mitchell, South Dakota, United States.

title: Disneyland
fact: Disneyland is a theme park at the Disneyland Resort in Anaheim, California, United States. It was the first theme park opened by the Walt Disney Company and the only one designed and constructed under the direct supervision of Walt Disney, opening on July 17, 1955.

title: Dome of the Rock
fact: The Dome of the Rock is an octagonal Islamic shrine at the center of the Al-Aqsa mosque compound on the Temple Mount in the Old City of Jerusalem.

title: Dubai Frame
fact: The Dubai Frame is an observatory, museum and monument in Zabeel Park, Dubai. It holds the record for the largest frame in the world. The building has a height of 150.24 meters and a width of 95.53 meters.

title: Edinburgh Castle
fact: Edinburgh Castle is a historic castle in Edinburgh, Scotland. It stands on Castle Rock, which has been occupied by humans since at least the Iron Age.

title: Eiffel Tower
fact: The Eiffel Tower is a lattice tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris, France. It is named after the engineer Gustave Eiffel, whose company designed and built the tower from 1887 to 1889.

title: Eilean Donan
fact: Eilean Donan is a small tidal island situated at the confluence of three sea lochs (Loch Duich, Loch Long and Loch Alsh) in the western Highlands of Scotland, about one kilometre (5⁄8 mi) from the village of Dornie.

title: Empire State Building
fact: The Empire State Building is a 102-story, supertall skyscraper in the Midtown South neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City, United States. The building was designed in the Art Deco style by Shreve, Lamb & Harmon and constructed between 1930 and 1931.

title: Fisherman's Bastion
fact: The Halászbástya or Fisherman's Bastion is one of the best known historical monuments in Budapest, located near the Buda Castle, in the Várkerület (Buda Castle District).

title: Forbidden City
fact: The Forbidden City is the imperial palace complex in the center of the Imperial City in Beijing, China. It was the residence of 24 Ming and Qing dynasty Emperors, and the center of political power in China for over 500 years from 1420 to 1924.

title: Four Corners Monument
fact: The Four Corners Monument marks the quadripoint in the Southwestern United States where the states of Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico, and Utah meet. It is the only point in the United States shared by four states, leading to the area being named the Four Corners region.

title: Frogner Park
fact: Frogner Park is a public park in the central West End borough of Frogner in Oslo, Norway. The park is historically part of Frogner Manor and is Oslo's largest park, open to the public at all times.

title: Gateway Arch
fact: The Gateway Arch is a 630-foot-tall (192 m) monument in St. Louis, Missouri, United States. Clad in stainless steel and built in the form of a weighted catenary arch, it is the world's tallest arch and Missouri's tallest accessible structure.

title: Gateway of India
fact: The Gateway of India is an arch-monument, completed in 1924, on the waterfront of Mumbai, Maharashtra, India.

title: Golden Gate Bridge
fact: The Golden Gate Bridge is a suspension bridge spanning the Golden Gate, the one-mile-wide (1.6 km) strait connecting San Francisco Bay and the Pacific Ocean in California, United States.

title: Golden Temple
fact: The Golden Temple is a gurdwara located in Amritsar, Punjab, India. It is the pre-eminent spiritual site of Sikhism and its holiest site. The gurdwara complex is a collection of buildings around the sanctum sanctorum and the sarovar (holy pool), known as the Amrit Sarovar.

title: Guggenheim Museum Bilbao
fact: The Guggenheim Museum Bilbao is a museum of modern and contemporary art in Bilbao, Biscay, Spain. It is one of several museums affiliated to the Solomon R. Guggenheim Foundation and features permanent and visiting exhibits of works by Spanish and international artists.

title: Guinness Storehouse
fact: Guinness Storehouse is a tourist attraction at St. James's Gate Brewery in Dublin, Ireland. Since opening in 2000, it has received over twenty million visitors. The Storehouse covers seven floors surrounding a glass atrium shaped in the form of a pint of Guinness.

title: Hagia Sophia
fact: Hagia Sophia, officially the Hagia Sophia Grand Mosque, is a mosque and a major cultural and historical site in Istanbul, Turkey. It was formerly a church (360–1453) and a museum (1935–2020).

title: Hallgrímskirkja
fact: Hallgrímskirkja is a Protestant Lutheran (Church of Iceland) parish church in Reykjavík, Iceland. At 74.5 metres (244 ft) tall, it is the largest church in Iceland and second tallest building in the country.

title: Hans Island
fact: Hans Island is an island in the centre of the Kennedy Channel of the Nares Strait in the high Arctic region, split between the Canadian territory of Nunavut and the Danish rigsdel (autonomous territory) of Greenland.

title: Haskell Free Library and Opera House
fact: The Haskell Free Library and Opera House is a Victorian building that straddles the Canada–United States border, in Rock Island (now part of Stanstead), Quebec, and Derby Line, Vermont, respectively.
story_label: Wikipedia: Haskell Free Library and Opera House

title: Hawa Mahal
fact: The Hawa Mahal is a palace in the city of Jaipur, Rajasthan, India. Built from red and pink sandstone, it is on the edge of the City Palace, Jaipur, and extends to the Zenana, or women's chambers.

title: Helsinki Cathedral
fact: Helsinki Cathedral is the Finnish Evangelical Lutheran cathedral of the Diocese of Helsinki, located in the neighborhood of Kruununhaka in the centre of Helsinki, Finland, at the Senate Square.

title: Himeji Castle
fact: Himeji Castle is a hilltop Japanese castle complex situated in Himeji, a city in Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan.

title: Hollywood Sign
fact: The Hollywood Sign is an American landmark and cultural icon overlooking Hollywood, Los Angeles. Originally the Hollywoodland Sign, it is on Mount Lee, above Beachwood Canyon in the Santa Monica Mountains.

title: Issyk-Kul
fact: Issyk-Kul or Ysyk-Köl is an endorheic saline lake in the western Tian Shan mountains in eastern Kyrgyzstan—just south of a dividing range separating Kyrgyzstan from Kazakhstan.

title: Itsukushima Shrine
fact: Itsukushima Shrine is a Shinto shrine on the island of Itsukushima (popularly known as Miyajima), best known for its "floating" torii. It is in the city of Hatsukaichi, in Hiroshima Prefecture in Japan, accessible from the mainland by ferry at Miyajimaguchi Station.

title: Jeddah Tower
fact: Jeddah Tower is a megatall skyscraper currently under construction in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. Located in the north of the city, it is the centrepiece of the Jeddah Economic City project.

title: Kaaba
fact: The Kaaba, also spelled Kaʽba, Kaʽbah or Kabah, sometimes referred to as al-Kaʽba al-Musharrafa, is a stone building at the center of Islam's most important mosque and holiest site, the Masjid al-Haram in Mecca, Saudi Arabia.

title: Kalyan Minaret
fact: The Kalyan Minaret is a minaret of the Po-i-Kalyan mosque complex in Bukhara, Uzbekistan and one of the most prominent landmarks in the city.

title: Keukenhof
fact: Keukenhof, also known as the Garden of Europe, is one of the world's largest flower gardens, situated in the municipality of Lisse, in the Netherlands.

title: Khiva
fact: Khiva is a district-level city of approximately 93,000 people in Khorazm Region, Uzbekistan. According to archaeological data, the city was established around 2,500 years ago. In 1997, Khiva celebrated its 2,500th anniversary.

title: Kinderdijk
fact: Kinderdijk is a town in the municipality of Molenlanden, in the province of South Holland, Netherlands. It is located about 15 km (9 miles) east of Rotterdam. Kinderdijk is situated in the Alblasserwaard polder at the confluence of the Lek and Noord rivers.

title: Kingdom Centre
fact: Kingdom Centre, formerly Kingdom Tower, is a 99-story, 302.3 m (992 ft) skyscraper in the al-Olaya district of Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. When completed in 2002, it overtook the 267-meter (876 ft) Faisaliah Tower as the tallest tower in Saudi Arabia.

title: Kinkaku-ji
fact: Kinkaku-ji, officially named Rokuon-ji, is a Zen Buddhist temple in Kyoto, Japan and a tourist attraction. It is designated as a World Heritage Site, a National Special Historic Site, a National Special Landscape, and one of the 17 Historic Monuments of Ancient Kyoto.

title: Las Vegas Strip
fact: The Las Vegas Strip is a stretch of Las Vegas Boulevard in Clark County, Nevada, that is known for its concentration of resort hotels and casinos.

title: Leaning Tower of Pisa
fact: The Leaning Tower of Pisa, or simply the Tower of Pisa (torre di Pisa), is the campanile, or freestanding bell tower, of Pisa Cathedral. It is known for its nearly four-degree lean, the result of an unstable foundation.

title: Little Diomede Island
fact: Little Diomede Island, formerly known as Krusenstern Island, after Adam Johann von Krusenstern, is an inhabited island of Alaska. It is the smaller of the two Diomede Islands located in the Bering Strait between the Alaskan mainland and Siberia.

title: Llívia
fact: Llívia is a town in the comarca of Cerdanya, province of Girona, Catalonia, Spain. It is a Spanish exclave surrounded by the French département of Pyrénées-Orientales. It is named after Livia, the wife of Augustus and matriarch of the Julio-Claudian dynasty.

title: Lotus Temple
fact: The Lotus Temple, also known as the Baháʼí House of Worship, New Delhi, is a Baháʼí House of Worship at Bahapur in south Delhi, India.

title: Magic Kingdom
fact: Magic Kingdom Park, or simply Magic Kingdom, is a theme park at Walt Disney World Resort in Bay Lake, Florida, near Orlando. It opened on October 1, 1971, and is owned and operated by the Walt Disney Company through its Experiences division.

title: Marina Bay Sands
fact: Marina Bay Sands (often colloquially shortened to 'MBS') is an integrated resort fronting Marina Bay in Singapore and a landmark of the city. At its opening in 2010, it was deemed the world's most expensive standalone casino property at S$8 billion (US$6.88 billion).

title: Märket
fact: Märket is a 3.3-hectare (8.2-acre) uninhabited skerry in the Baltic Sea shared by Sweden and Finland, with a lighthouse as its salient humanmade feature.

title: Meenakshi Temple
fact: Meenakshi Temple, also known as Meenakshi Sundareswarar Temple, is a historic Hindu temple located on the southern bank of the Vaigai River in Madurai, Tamil Nadu, India. It is dedicated to Meenakshi, a form of Parvati, and her consort Sundareswarar (Shiva).

title: Mehrangarh
fact: Mehrangarh is a historic fort located in Jodhpur, Rajasthan, India. It stands on a hilltop, rising about 122 m (400 ft) above the surrounding plains, and the complex spans 1,200 acres (486 hectares).

title: Mount Rushmore
fact: The Mount Rushmore National Memorial is a national memorial featuring a colossal sculpture carved into the granite face of Mount Rushmore in the Black Hills, about 2 mi (3 km) southwest of Keystone, South Dakota, United States.

title: Museum of Islamic Art, Doha
fact: The Museum of Islamic Art is a museum at one end of the seven-kilometer-long (4.3 mi) Corniche in Doha, Qatar. As per architect I. M. Pei's specifications, the museum is built on an island on an artificial projecting peninsula near the traditional dhow harbor.
story_label: Wikipedia: Museum of Islamic Art, Doha

title: Mykonos windmills
fact: The Mykonos windmills are an iconic feature of the Greek island of the Mykonos. The island is one of the Cyclades islands, which neighbour Delos in the Aegean Sea.

title: Neft Daşları
fact: Neft Daşları is an industrial settlement in Baku, Azerbaijan. The settlement forms part of the municipality of Çilov-Neft Daşları in the Pirallahı raion. It lies 86 km (53 mi) away from Baku and 39 km (24 mi) from the nearest mainland shore in the Caspian Sea.

title: Nyhavn
fact: Nyhavn is a 17th-century waterfront, canal and entertainment district in Copenhagen, Denmark.

title: Palm Jumeirah
fact: The Palm Jumeirah, also known as the Palm Islands, is an archipelago of artificial islands on the Persian Gulf in Jumeirah, Dubai, United Arab Emirates.

title: Park Güell
fact: Park Güell is a complex of parks and gardens in Barcelona with architectural elements, located in the La Salut neighborhood of the Gràcia district in Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain.

title: Parthenon
fact: The Parthenon is a former temple on the Athenian Acropolis, Greece, that was dedicated to the goddess Athena.

title: Peleș Castle
fact: Peleș Castle is a Neo-Renaissance palace in the Royal Domain of Sinaia in the Carpathian Mountains, near Sinaia, in Prahova County, Romania, on an existing medieval route linking Transylvania and Wallachia, built between 1873 and 1914. Its inauguration was held in 1883.

title: Peterhof Palace
fact: The Peterhof Palace is a series of palaces and gardens located in Petergof, Saint Petersburg, Russia, commissioned by Peter the Great as a direct response to the Palace of Versailles by Louis XIV of France.

title: Petronas Towers
fact: The Petronas Towers, also known as the Petronas Twin Towers and colloquially the KLCC Twin Towers, are an interlinked pair of 88-storey supertall skyscrapers in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, standing at 451.9 m (1,483 ft).

title: Lengai, Ol Doinyo
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,962 m in Tanzania. Erupting as of Sep 2026. The symmetrical Ol Doinyo Lengai is the only volcano known to have erupted carbonatite tephras and lavas in historical time.

title: Nyamulagira
fact: Shield volcano, 3,058 m in DR Congo. Erupting as of Sep 2026. Africa's most active volcano, Nyamulagira, is a massive high-potassium basaltic shield about 25 km N of Lake Kivu and 13 km NNW of the steep-sided Nyiragongo volcano.

title: Heard
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,745 m in Australia. Erupting as of Sep 2026. Heard Island on the Kerguelen Plateau in the southern Indian Ocean consists primarily of the emergent portion of two volcanic structures.

title: Tofua
fact: Caldera, 515 m in Tonga. Erupting as of Sep 2026. The low, forested Tofua Island in the central part of the Tonga Islands group is the emergent summit of a large stratovolcano that was seen in eruption by Captain Cook in 1774.

title: Home Reef
fact: Stratovolcano, -10 m in Tonga. Erupting as of Sep 2026. Home Reef, a submarine volcano midway between Metis Shoal and Late Island in the central Tonga islands, was first reported active in the mid-19th century, when an ephemeral island formed.

title: Savaii
fact: Shield volcano, 1,858 m in Samoa. Last erupted 1911. Savai'i, the largest and highest of the Samoan islands, consists of a massive basaltic shield volcano constructed along a WNW-ESE-trending rift zone that splits into two rifts on the east side of the 75-km-long…

title: Manam
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,807 m in Papua New Guinea. Erupting as of Sep 2026. The 10-km-wide island of Manam, lying 13 km off the northern coast of mainland Papua New Guinea, is one of the country's most active volcanoes.

title: Langila
fact: Complex volcano, 1,330 m in Papua New Guinea. Erupting as of Sep 2026. Langila, one of the most active volcanoes of New Britain, consists of a group of four small overlapping composite basaltic-andesitic cones on the lower E flank of the extinct Talawe volcano in the Cape…

title: Bagana
fact: Lava cone, 1,855 m in Papua New Guinea. Erupting as of Sep 2026. Bagana volcano, in a remote portion of central Bougainville Island, is frequently active. This massive symmetrical cone was largely constructed by an accumulation of viscous andesitic lava flows.

title: Ambae
fact: Shield volcano, 1,496 m in Vanuatu. Erupting as of Sep 2026. The island of Ambae, also known as Aoba, is a massive 2,500 km3 basaltic shield that is the most voluminous volcano of the New Hebrides archipelago.

title: Yasur
fact: Stratovolcano, 361 m in Vanuatu. Erupting as of Sep 2026. Yasur has exhibited essentially continuous Strombolian and Vulcanian activity at least since Captain Cook observed ash eruptions in 1774. This style of activity may have continued for the past 800 years.

title: Sinabung
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,460 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 2021. Gunung Sinabung is a Pleistocene-to-Holocene stratovolcano with many lava flows on its flanks. The migration of summit vents along a N-S line gives the summit crater complex an elongated form.

title: Marapi
fact: Complex volcano, 2,885 m in Indonesia. Erupting as of Sep 2026. Gunung Marapi, not to be confused with the better-known Merapi volcano on Java, is Sumatra's most active volcano. This massive complex stratovolcano rises 2,000 m above the Bukittinggi Plain in the Padang Highlands.

title: Galunggung
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,168 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 1984. The forested slopes of Galunggung in western Java SE of Bandung are cut by a 2-km-wide collapse scarp open towards the ESE.

title: Kelud
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,730 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 2014. The relatively inconspicuous Kelud stratovolcano contains a summit crater lake that has been the source of some of Indonesia's most deadly eruptions.

title: Semeru
fact: Stratovolcano, 3,657 m in Indonesia. Erupting as of Sep 2026. Semeru, the highest volcano on Java, and one of its most active, lies at the southern end of a volcanic massif extending north to the Tengger caldera.

title: Agung
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,997 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 2022. Symmetrical Agung stratovolcano, Bali's highest and most sacred mountain, towers over the eastern end of the island.

title: Lewotolok
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,431 m in Indonesia. Erupting as of Sep 2026. The Lewotolok (or Lewotolo) stratovolcano occupies the eastern end of an elongated peninsula extending north into the Flores Sea, connected to Lembata Island by a narrow isthmus.

title: Dukono
fact: Complex volcano, 1,273 m in Indonesia. Erupting as of Sep 2026. The Dukono complex in northern Halmahera is on an edifice with a broad, low profile containing multiple peaks and overlapping craters.

title: Ibu
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,357 m in Indonesia. Erupting as of Sep 2026. The truncated summit of Gunung Ibu stratovolcano along the NW coast of Halmahera Island has large nested summit craters. The inner crater, 1 km wide and 400 m deep, has contained several small crater lakes.

title: Kanlaon
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,422 m in Philippines. Erupting as of Sep 2026. Kanlaon volcano forms the highest point on the Philippine island of Negros. The massive andesitic stratovolcano is covered with fissure-controlled pyroclastic cones and craters, many of which are filled by lakes.

title: Suwanosejima
fact: Stratovolcano, 796 m in Japan. Erupting as of Sep 2026. The 8-km-long island of Suwanosejima in the northern Ryukyu Islands consists of an andesitic stratovolcano with two active summit craters.

title: Pagan
fact: Stratovolcano, 570 m in United States. Last erupted 2021. Pagan Island, the largest and one of the most active of the Mariana Islands volcanoes, consists of two stratovolcanoes connected by a narrow isthmus.

title: Krasheninnikov
fact: Caldera, 1,816 m in Russia. Erupting as of Sep 2026. The late Pleistocene to Holocene Krasheninnikov volcano is comprised of two overlapping stratovolcanoes within a 9 x 10 km Pleistocene caldera.

title: Sheveluch
fact: Stratovolcano, 3,283 m in Russia. Erupting as of Sep 2026. The high, isolated massif of Sheveluch volcano rises above the lowlands NNE of the Kliuchevskaya volcano group.

title: Michoacan-Guanajuato
fact: Volcanic field, 3,860 m in Mexico. Last erupted 1952. The widespread Michoacán-Guanajuato volcanic field contains over 1,400 vents, including the historically active cinder cones of Parícutin and Jorullo…

title: Chichon, El
fact: Lava dome, 1,150 m in Mexico. Last erupted 1982. El Chichón is a small trachyandesitic tuff cone and lava dome complex in an isolated part of the Chiapas region in SE México.

title: Santa Maria
fact: Stratovolcano, 3,745 m in Guatemala. Erupting as of Sep 2026. Symmetrical, forest-covered Santa María volcano is part of a chain of large stratovolcanoes that rise above the Pacific coastal plain of Guatemala.

title: Fuego
fact: Stratovolcano, 3,799 m in Guatemala. Erupting as of Sep 2026. Volcán Fuego, one of Central America's most active volcanoes, is also one of three large stratovolcanoes overlooking Guatemala's former capital, Antigua.

title: Masaya
fact: Caldera, 594 m in Nicaragua. Erupting as of Sep 2026. Masaya volcano in Nicaragua has erupted frequently since the time of the Spanish Conquistadors, when an active lava lake prompted attempts to extract the volcano's molten "gold" until it was found to be basalt rock upon…

title: Poas
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,697 m in Costa Rica. Erupting as of Sep 2026. The broad vegetated edifice of Poás, one of the most active volcanoes of Costa Rica, contains three craters along a N-S line.

title: Ruiz, Nevado del
fact: Stratovolcano, 5,279 m in Colombia. Erupting as of Sep 2026. Nevado del Ruiz is a broad, glacier-covered volcano in central Colombia that covers more than 200 km2.

title: Purace
fact: Stratovolcano, 4,650 m in Colombia. Erupting as of Sep 2026. Puracé is an active andesitic volcano with a 600-m-diameter summit crater at the NW end of the Los Coconucos Volcanic Chain.

title: Reventador
fact: Stratovolcano, 3,562 m in Ecuador. Erupting as of Sep 2026. Volcán El Reventador is the most frequently active of a chain of Ecuadorian volcanoes in the Cordillera Real, well east of the principal volcanic axis.

title: Sangay
fact: Stratovolcano, 5,286 m in Ecuador. Erupting as of Sep 2026. The isolated Sangay volcano, located east of the Andean crest, is the southernmost of Ecuador's volcanoes and its most active.

title: Wolf
fact: Shield volcano, 1,710 m in Ecuador. Last erupted 2022. Volcán Wolf, the highest volcano of the Galápagos Islands, straddles the equator at the north end of the archipelago's largest island, Isabela.

title: Sabancaya
fact: Stratovolcano, 5,960 m in Peru. Erupting as of Sep 2026. Sabancaya, located in the saddle NE of Ampato and SE of Hualca Hualca volcanoes, is the youngest of these volcanic centers and the only one to have erupted in historical time.

title: Puyehue-Cordon Caulle
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,236 m in Chile. Last erupted 2012. The Puyehue-Cordón Caulle volcanic complex (PCCVC) is a large NW-SE-trending late-Pleistocene to Holocene basaltic-to-rhyolitic transverse volcanic chain SE of Lago Ranco.

title: Calbuco
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,974 m in Chile. Last erupted 2015. Calbuco is one of the most active volcanoes of the southern Chilean Andes, along with its neighbor, Osorno. The late-Pleistocene to Holocene andesitic volcano is immediately SE of Lake Llanquihué in the Chilean lake district.

title: Chaiten
fact: Caldera, 1,122 m in Chile. Last erupted 2011. Chaitén is a small caldera (~3 km in diameter) located 10 km NE of the town of Chaitén on the Gulf of Corcovado. Multiple explosive eruptions throughout the Holocene have been identified.

title: Pelee
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,372 m in France. Last erupted 1932. Montagne Pelée forms the northern end of the island of Martinique. Three major edifice failures since the late Pleistocene, the last about 9,000 years ago…

title: Soufriere St. Vincent
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,220 m in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines. Last erupted 2021. Soufrière St. Vincent is the northernmost and youngest volcano on St. Vincent Island. The NE rim of the 1.6-km wide summit crater is cut by a crater formed in 1812.

title: Hekla
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,490 m in Iceland. Last erupted 2000. One of Iceland's most prominent and active volcanoes, Hekla lies near the southern end of the eastern rift zone.

title: Grimsvotn
fact: Caldera, 1,719 m in Iceland. Last erupted 2011. Grímsvötn, Iceland's most frequently active volcano in recent history, lies largely beneath the vast Vatnajökull icecap.

title: Jan Mayen
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,197 m in Norway. Last erupted 1985. Remote Jan Mayen Island, located in the Norwegian Sea along the Jan Mayen Ridge about 650 km NE of Iceland, consists of two volcanic complexes separated by a narrow isthmus.

title: Hierro
fact: Shield volcano, 1,500 m in Spain. Last erupted 2012. The triangular island of Hierro is the SW-most and least studied of the Canary Islands. The massive shield volcano is truncated by a large NW-facing escarpment formed as a result of gravitational collapse of El Golfo volcano…

title: Tenerife
fact: Stratovolcano, 3,715 m in Spain. Last erupted 1909. The large triangular island of Tenerife is composed of a complex of overlapping Miocene-to-Quaternary stratovolcanoes.

title: Saunders
fact: Stratovolcano, 843 m in United Kingdom. Erupting as of Sep 2026. Saunders Island consists of a large central volcanic edifice intersected by two seamount chains, as shown by bathymetric mapping (Leat et al., 2013).

title: Fogo
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,829 m in Cabo Verde. Last erupted 2015. The island of Fogo consists of a single massive stratovolcano that is the most prominent of the Cape Verde Islands.

title: Hayli Gubbi
fact: Shield volcano, 493 m in Ethiopia. Last erupted 2025. Hayli Gubbi is the southernmost volcano of the Erta Ale Range. Recent tectonism has created a NW-SE graben across the summit, with a 380-m-diameter scoria cone at the summit and a 260-m-diameter crater displaying fumarolic…

title: Asamayama
fact: Complex volcano, 2,568 m in Japan. Last erupted 2019. Asamayama, Honshu's most active volcano, overlooks the resort town of Karuizawa, 140 km NW of Tokyo. The volcano is located at the junction of the Izu-Marianas and NE Japan volcanic arcs.

title: Hudson, Cerro
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,905 m in Chile. Last erupted 2011. The ice-filled, 10-km-wide caldera of Cerro Hudson volcano was not recognized until its first 20th-century eruption in 1971.

title: Terceira
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,023 m in Portugal. Last erupted 2000. Terceira Island contains multiple stratovolcanoes constructed along a prominent ESE-WNW fissure zone that cuts across the island.

title: Lewotobi
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,703 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 2026. The Lewotobi edifice in eastern Flores Island is composed of the two adjacent Lewotobi Laki-laki and Lewotobi Perempuan stratovolcanoes (the "husband and wife"). Their summits are less than 2 km apart along a NW-SE line.

title: Tolbachik
fact: Shield volcano, 3,611 m in Russia. Last erupted 2013. The massive Tolbachik volcano is located at the southern end of the Kliuchevskaya volcano group. The massif is composed of two overlapping, but morphologically distinct, volcanoes.

title: Sarychev Peak
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,496 m in Russia. Last erupted 2021. Sarychev Peak, one of the most active volcanoes of the Kuril Islands, occupies the NW end of Matua Island in the central Kuriles.

title: Augustine
fact: Lava dome, 1,218 m in United States. Last erupted 2006. Augustine volcano, rising above Kamishak Bay in the southern Cook Inlet about 290 km SW of Anchorage, is the most active volcano of the eastern Aleutian arc.

title: Asosan
fact: Caldera, 1,592 m in Japan. Last erupted 2021. The 24-km-wide Asosan caldera was formed during four major explosive eruptions from 300,000 to 90,000 years ago. These produced voluminous pyroclastic flows that covered much of Kyushu.

title: Katla
fact: Fissure vent, 1,490 m in Iceland. Last erupted 1918. Katla volcano, located near the southern end of Iceland's eastern volcanic zone, is hidden beneath the Myrdalsjökull icecap.

title: Kerinci
fact: Stratovolcano, 3,800 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 2024. Gunung Kerinci in central Sumatra forms Indonesia's highest volcano and is one of the most active in Sumatra. It is capped by an unvegetated young summit cone that was constructed NE of an older crater remnant.

title: Tungurahua
fact: Stratovolcano, 5,023 m in Ecuador. Last erupted 2016. Tungurahua, a steep-sided andesitic-dacitic stratovolcano that towers more than 3 km above its northern base, is one of Ecuador's most active volcanoes.

title: Rabaul
fact: Caldera, 688 m in Papua New Guinea. Last erupted 2014. The low-lying Rabaul caldera on the tip of the Gazelle Peninsula at the NE end of New Britain forms a broad sheltered harbor utilized by what was the island's largest city prior to a major eruption in 1994.

title: Avachinsky
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,717 m in Russia. Last erupted 2001. Avachinsky, one of Kamchatka's most active volcanoes, rises above Petropavlovsk, Kamchatka's largest city.

title: Nabro
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,218 m in Eritrea. Last erupted 2012. The Nabro stratovolcano is the highest volcano in the Danakil depression of northern Ethiopia and Eritrea, at the SE end of the Danakil Alps.

title: Ulawun
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,334 m in Papua New Guinea. Last erupted 2025. The symmetrical basaltic-to-andesitic Ulawun stratovolcano is the highest volcano of the Bismarck arc, and one of Papua New Guinea's most frequently active.

title: Okmok
fact: Shield volcano, 1,073 m in United States. Last erupted 2008. The basaltic Okmok shield volcano forms the NE end of Umnak Island in the Aleutian Islands.

title: Colima
fact: Stratovolcano, 3,850 m in Mexico. Last erupted 2019. The Colima complex is the most prominent volcanic center of the western Mexican Volcanic Belt.

title: Galeras
fact: Complex volcano, 4,276 m in Colombia. Last erupted 2014. Galeras, a stratovolcano with a large breached caldera located immediately west of the city of Pasto, is one of Colombia's most frequently active volcanoes.

title: Lascar
fact: Stratovolcano, 5,592 m in Chile. Last erupted 2026. Láscar is the most active volcano of the northern Chilean Andes. The andesitic-to-dacitic stratovolcano contains six overlapping summit craters. Prominent lava flows descend its NW flanks.

title: Meru
fact: Stratovolcano, 4,550 m in Tanzania. Last erupted 1910. Meru has a conical profile when viewed from the west, but there is a 4-km-wide collapse crater to the E. The summit collapse is associated with the early Holocene Momella event that resulted in debris avalanche and lahar…

title: Awu
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,318 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 2004. The massive Gunung Awu stratovolcano occupies the northern end of Great Sangihe Island, the largest of the Sangihe arc.

title: Unzendake
fact: Complex volcano, 1,483 m in Japan. Last erupted 1996. The massive Unzendake volcanic complex comprises much of the Shimabara Peninsula east of the city of Nagasaki. An E-W graben, 30-40 km long, extends across the peninsula.

title: Copahue
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,953 m in Chile-Argentina. Last erupted 2024. Volcán Copahue is an elongated composite cone constructed along the Chile-Argentina border within the 6.5 x 8.5 km wide Trapa-Trapa caldera that formed between 0.6 and 0.4 million years ago near the NW margin of the…

title: Fayal
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,041 m in Portugal. Last erupted 1958. The island of Fayal, also spelled Faial, is the nearest of the central Azorean islands to the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.

title: Ontakesan
fact: Complex volcano, 3,067 m in Japan. Last erupted 2014. The massive Ontakesan stratovolcano, the second highest volcano in Japan, lies at the southern end of the Northern Japan Alps.

title: Arenal
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,670 m in Costa Rica. Last erupted 2010. Conical Volcán Arenal is the youngest stratovolcano in Costa Rica and one of its most active.

title: Novarupta
fact: Caldera, 841 m in United States. Last erupted 1912. Novarupta, the least topographically prominent volcano in the Katmai area, was formed during a major eruption in 1912.

title: Bardarbunga
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,000 m in Iceland. Last erupted 2015. The large central volcano of Bárðarbunga lies beneath the NW part of the Vatnajökull icecap, NW of Grímsvötn volcano, and contains a subglacial 700-m-deep caldera.

title: Askja
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,080 m in Iceland. Last erupted 1961. Askja is a large basaltic central volcano that forms the Dyngjufjöll massif. It is truncated by three overlapping calderas, the largest of which is 8 km wide and may have been produced primarily from subglacial ring-fracture…

title: Changbaishan
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,744 m in China-North Korea. Last erupted 1903. Massive Changbaishan stratovolcano, is located along the China/Korea border. A 5-km-wide, 850-m-deep summit caldera is filled by Lake Tianchi (Sky Lake).

title: Huila, Nevado del
fact: Stratovolcano, 5,364 m in Colombia. Last erupted 2012. Nevado del Huila, the highest peak in the Colombian Andes, is an elongated N-S-trending volcanic chain mantled by a glacier icecap. The andesitic-dacitic volcano was constructed within a 10-km-wide caldera.

title: Fournaise, Piton de la
fact: Shield volcano, 2,632 m in France. Last erupted 2026. Piton de la Fournaise is a massive basaltic shield volcano on the French island of Réunion in the western Indian Ocean.

title: Tongariro
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,978 m in New Zealand. Last erupted 2012. Tongariro is a large volcanic massif, located immediately NE of Ruapehu volcano, that is composed of more than a dozen composite cones constructed over a period of 275,000 years.

title: Ruang
fact: Stratovolcano, 703 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 2024. Ruang volcano is the southernmost volcano in the Sangihe Island arc, north of Sulawesi Island; it is not the better known Raung volcano on Java.

title: Chachadake [Tiatia]
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,772 m in Japan - administered by Russia. Last erupted 1981. The symmetrical Chachadake, also known as Tiatia, is on the SE side of northern Kunashir Island in the southern Kuriles.

title: Chikurachki
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,781 m in Russia. Last erupted 2023. Chikurachki, the highest volcano on Paramushir Island in the northern Kuriles, is a relatively small cone constructed on a high Pleistocene edifice.

title: Irazu
fact: Stratovolcano, 3,436 m in Costa Rica. Last erupted 1977. The massive Irazú volcano in Costa Rica, immediately E of the capital city of San José, covers an area of 500 km2 and is vegetated to within a few hundred meters of its broad summit crater complex.

title: Villarrica
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,847 m in Chile. Last erupted 2025. The glacier-covered Villarrica stratovolcano, in the northern Lakes District of central Chile, is ~15 km south of the city of Pucon.

title: Sao Jorge
fact: Fissure vent, 1,053 m in Portugal. Last erupted 1902. The dominantly basaltic São Jorge Island is 55 km long and 6.5 km wide. It was formed by fissure eruptions beginning in the eastern part of the island.

title: Lanzarote
fact: Fissure vent, 670 m in Spain. Last erupted 1824. The 60-km-long island of Lanzarote at the NE end of the Canary Islands contains the largest concentration of youthful volcanism in the Canaries.

title: Karthala
fact: Shield volcano, 2,350 m in Union of the Comoros. Last erupted 2007. The southernmost and largest of the two shield volcanoes forming Grand Comore Island, Karthala has two overlapping 3-4 km summit calderas generated by repeated collapse.

title: Ambrym
fact: Shield(pyroclastic), 1,334 m in Vanuatu. Last erupted 2024. Ambrym is a large basaltic volcano with a 12-km-wide caldera formed during a major Plinian eruption with dacitic pyroclastic flows about 1,900 years ago.

title: Soufriere Hills
fact: Stratovolcano, 915 m in United Kingdom. Last erupted 2013. The complex, dominantly andesitic Soufrière Hills volcano occupies the southern half of the island of Montserrat. The summit area consists primarily of a series of lava domes emplaced along an ESE-trending zone.

title: Pacaya
fact: Complex volcano, 2,569 m in Guatemala. Last erupted 2021. Eruptions from Pacaya are frequently visible from Guatemala City, the nation's capital. This complex basaltic volcano was constructed just outside the southern topographic rim of the 14 x 16 km Pleistocene Amatitlán…

title: Misti, El
fact: Stratovolcano, 5,793 m in Peru. Last erupted 1985. El Misti is a symmetrical andesitic stratovolcano with nested summit craters immediately NE of the city of Arequipa, Peru.

title: Campi Flegrei
fact: Caldera, 458 m in Italy. Last erupted 1538. Campi Flegrei is a 13-km-wide caldera that encompasses part of Naples and extends to the south beneath the Gulf of Pozzuoli.

title: Momotombo
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,270 m in Nicaragua. Last erupted 2016. Momotombo is a young stratovolcano that rises prominently above the NW shore of Lake Managua, forming one of Nicaragua's most familiar landmarks.

title: Guagua Pichincha
fact: Stratovolcano, 4,784 m in Ecuador. Last erupted 2002. Guagua Pichincha and the older Pleistocene Rucu Pichincha stratovolcanoes form a broad volcanic massif that rises immediately W of Ecuador's capital city, Quito.

title: Bulusan
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,535 m in Philippines. Last erupted 2025. Luzon's southernmost volcano, Bulusan, was constructed along the rim of the 11-km-diameter dacitic-to-rhyolitic Irosin caldera, which was formed about 36,000 years ago.

title: Bezymianny
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,882 m in Russia. Last erupted 2025. The modern Bezymianny, much smaller than its massive neighbors Kamen and Kliuchevskoi on the Kamchatka Peninsula…

title: Llaima
fact: Stratovolcano, 3,125 m in Chile. Last erupted 2009. Llaima, one of Chile's largest and most active volcanoes, contains two main historically active craters, one at the summit and the other, Pichillaima, to the SE.

title: La Palma
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,426 m in Spain. Last erupted 2021. The 47-km-long wedge-shaped island of La Palma, the NW-most of the Canary Islands, is composed of two large volcanic centers.

title: Barren Island
fact: Stratovolcano, 354 m in India. Last erupted 2026. Barren Island, a possession of India in the Andaman Sea about 135 km NE of Port Blair in the Andaman Islands, is the only historically active volcano along the N-S volcanic arc extending between Sumatra and Burma (Myanmar).

title: Izu-Oshima
fact: Stratovolcano, 758 m in Japan. Last erupted 1990. Izu-Oshima volcano in Sagami Bay, east of the Izu Peninsula, is the northernmost of the Izu Islands. The broad, low stratovolcano forms an 11 x 13 km island constructed over the remnants of three older dissected stratovolcanoes.

title: Anatahan
fact: Stratovolcano, 790 m in United States. Last erupted 2008. The elongate, 9-km-long island of Anatahan in the central Mariana Islands consists of a large stratovolcano with a 2.3 x 5 km compound summit caldera.

title: Redoubt
fact: Stratovolcano, 3,108 m in United States. Last erupted 2009. Redoubt is a glacier-covered stratovolcano with a breached summit crater in Lake Clark National Park about 170 km SW of Anchorage.

title: Krafla
fact: Caldera, 800 m in Iceland. Last erupted 1984. The Krafla volcanic system in the Northern Volcanic Zone (NVZ) of Iceland is about 100 km long, consisting of a fissure swarm and a central volcano with a 7 x 9 km caldera formed about 110,000 years ago that deposited a rhyolitic…

title: Alaid
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,285 m in Russia. Last erupted 2022. The highest and northernmost volcano of the Kuril Islands, Alaid is a symmetrical stratovolcano when viewed from the north, but has a 1.5-km-wide summit crater that is breached open to the south.

title: Aconcagua
fact: Aconcagua is a mountain in the Principal Cordillera of the Andes range, located in Mendoza Province, Argentina. With a summit elevation of 6,967.15 metres (22,858.1 feet), it is the highest mountain outside Asia.

title: Annapurna
fact: Annapurna is a mountain situated in the Annapurna mountain range of Gandaki Province, north-central Nepal. It is the 10th highest mountain in the world at 8,091 metres (26,545 ft) above sea level and is well known for the difficulty and danger involved in its ascent.

title: Atacama Desert
fact: The Atacama Desert is a desert plateau on the Pacific coast of South America, stretching along a 1,600-kilometre-long (1,000-mile) strip of land in northern Chile, west of the Andes.

title: Ben Nevis
fact: Ben Nevis is the highest mountain in Scotland, the United Kingdom, and the British Isles. Ben Nevis stands at the western end of the Grampian Mountains in the Highland region of Lochaber, close to the town of Fort William.

title: Bingham Canyon Mine
fact: The Bingham Canyon Mine, more commonly known as Kennecott Copper Mine among locals, is an open-pit mining operation extracting a large porphyry copper deposit southwest of Salt Lake City, Utah, in the Oquirrh Mountains.

title: Blood Falls
fact: Blood Falls is an outflow of an iron(III) oxide–tainted plume of saltwater, flowing from the tongue of Taylor Glacier onto the ice-covered surface of West Lake Bonney in the Taylor Valley of the McMurdo Dry Valleys in Victoria Land, East Antarctica.

title: Calypso Deep
fact: Calypso Deep is the deepest point in the Mediterranean Sea, located in the Hellenic Trench in the Ionian Sea, 62.6 km south-west of Pylos, Greece, with a maximum depth of approximately 5,200 m (17,100 ft).

title: Cape Agulhas
fact: Cape Agulhas is a rocky headland in Western Cape, South Africa. It is both the southernmost point of South Africa, the geographic southern tip of Africa and the beginning of the traditional dividing line between the Atlantic and Indian oceans according to the International…

title: Cape Dezhnyov
fact: Cape Dezhnyov or Cape Dezhnev, formerly known as East Cape or Cape Vostochny, is a cape that forms the easternmost mainland point of Asia. It is located on the Chukchi Peninsula in the very sparsely populated Chukotka Autonomous Okrug of Russia.

title: Cape Horn
fact: Cape Horn is the southernmost headland of the Tierra del Fuego archipelago of southern Chile, and is located on the small Hornos Island.

title: Cave of the Crystals
fact: Cave of the Crystals, also known as Naica Cave or the Giant Crystal Cave, is a cave connected to the Naica Mine at a depth of 300 metres (980 ft), in Naica, Chihuahua, Mexico.

title: Chimborazo
fact: Chimborazo is a stratovolcano in Ecuador and the Cordillera Occidental range of the Andes. Its last known eruption is believed to have occurred around AD 550. Chimborazo is the highest mountain in Ecuador and the 39th-highest peak in the entire Andes.

title: Cho Oyu
fact: Cho Oyu is the sixth-highest mountain in the world at 8,188 metres (26,864 ft) above sea level. Cho Oyu means 'Turquoise Goddess' in Tibetan. The mountain is the westernmost major peak of the Khumbu sub-section of the Mahalangur Himalaya 20 km (12 mi) west of Mount Everest.

title: Crater Lake
fact: Crater Lake (Klamath: Giiwas) is a volcanic crater lake in south-central Oregon in the Western United States. It is the main feature of Crater Lake National Park and is a tourist attraction known for its deep blue color and water clarity.

title: Dallol (hydrothermal system)
fact: Dallol is a unique, terrestrial hydrothermal system around a cinder cone volcano in the Danakil Depression, northeast of the Erta Ale Range in Ethiopia.

title: Danyang–Kunshan Grand Bridge
fact: The Danyang–Kunshan Grand Bridge is a 164.8-kilometre-long (102.4 mi) viaduct on the Beijing–Shanghai High-Speed Railway. It is the longest bridge in the world since its designation by Guinness World Record in 2011.

title: Dead Sea
fact: The Dead Sea, also known by other names, is a landlocked salt lake bordered by Jordan to the east, the West Bank to the west and Israel to the southwest. It lies in the endorheic basin of the Jordan Rift Valley, and its main tributary is the Jordan River.

title: Denali
fact: Denali, federally designated as Mount McKinley, is the highest mountain peak in North America, with a summit elevation of 20,310 feet (6,190 m) above sea level.

title: Dhaulagiri
fact: Dhaulagiri, located in Nepal, is the seventh highest mountain in the world at 8,167 metres (26,795 ft) above sea level, and the highest mountain within the borders of a single country. Dhaulagiri I is also the highest point of the Gandaki river basin.

title: Eisriesenwelt
fact: The Eisriesenwelt is a natural limestone and ice cave located in Werfen, Austria, about 40 km south of Salzburg. The cave is inside the Hochkogel mountain in the Tennengebirge section of the Alps.

title: Furnace Creek, California
fact: Furnace Creek is a census-designated place (CDP) in Inyo County, California, United States. The population was 136 at the 2020 census, up from 24 at the 2010 census. The elevation of the village is 190 feet (58 m) below sea level.

title: Gasherbrum I
fact: Gasherbrum I, originally surveyed as K5, and also known as Hidden Peak, is the 11th highest mountain in the world at 8,080 metres (26,510 ft) above sea level.

title: General Sherman Tree
fact: The General Sherman Tree is a giant sequoia (Sequoiadendron giganteum) tree in the Giant Forest of Sequoia National Park in Tulare County, California. By volume, it is the largest known living single-stem tree on Earth.

title: Gotthard Base Tunnel
fact: The Gotthard Base Tunnel is a railway tunnel through the Alps in Switzerland. It opened in June 2016 and full service began the following December.

title: Great Barrier Reef
fact: The Great Barrier Reef is the world's largest coral reef system, composed of over 2,900 individual reefs and 900 islands stretching for over 2,300 kilometres (1,400 mi) over an area of approximately 344,400 square kilometres (133,000 mi2).

title: Great Blue Hole
fact: The Great Blue Hole is a large marine sinkhole off the coast of Belize. It lies near the center of Lighthouse Reef, a small atoll 70 km (43 mi) from the mainland and Belize City. The hole is circular in shape, 318 m (1,043 ft) across and 124 m (407 ft) deep.

title: Hang Sơn Đoòng
fact: Sơn Đoòng Cave, in Phong Nha–Kẻ Bàng National Park, Quảng Trị province, Vietnam, is the world's largest natural cave.

title: Huascarán
fact: Huascarán, Nevado Huascarán or Mataraju is a mountain located in Yungay Province, Ancash Department, Peru. It is situated in the Cordillera Blanca range of the western Andes.

title: Hyperion (tree)
fact: Hyperion is a coast redwood (Sequoia sempervirens D.Don, Endl.) tree in California, which is the world's tallest known living tree, measured at 116.22 metres (381.3 ft) tall in 2026. Hyperion was discovered on August 25, 2006, by the naturalists Chris Atkins and Michael Taylor.

title: Iguazu Falls
fact: Iguazú Falls or Iguaçu Falls are waterfalls of the Iguazu River on the border of the Argentine province of Misiones and the Brazilian state of Paraná. Together, they make up the largest waterfall system in the world. The falls divide the river into the upper and lower Iguazu.

title: Inga Falls
fact: Inga Falls is a rapid 40 kilometres (25 mi) from Matadi in the Democratic Republic of the Congo where the Congo River drops 96 metres (315 ft) over the course of 15 kilometres (9.3 mi). The falls are part of a larger group of rapids in the lower Congo River.

title: K2
fact: K2, also known as Mount Godwin-Austen, at 8,611 metres (28,251 ft) above sea level, is the second-highest mountain on Earth, after Mount Everest at 8,849 metres (29,032 ft).

title: Kaffeklubben Island
fact: Kaffeklubben Island or Coffee Club Island is an uninhabited island lying off the northern shore of Greenland. It contains the northernmost undisputed point of land on Earth.

title: Kangchenjunga
fact: Kangchenjunga is the third-highest mountain in the world. Its summit lies at 8,586 m (28,169 ft) in a section of the Himalayas, the Kangchenjunga Himal, which is bounded in the west by the Tamur River, in the north by the Lhonak River and Jongsang La…

title: Kermadec Trench
fact: The Kermadec Trench is a linear ocean trench in the south Pacific Ocean. It stretches about 1,000 km (620 mi) from the Louisville Seamount Chain in the north (26°S) to the Hikurangi Plateau in the south (37°S), north-east of New Zealand's North Island.

title: Khone Phapheng Falls
fact: The Khone Falls and Pha Pheng Falls together form a waterfall located in Champasak Province on the Mekong River in southern Laos, near the border with Cambodia.

title: Kjeragbolten
fact: Kjeragbolten (English: Kjerag Bolt) is a boulder on the mountain Kjerag in the eastern part of Sandnes Municipality in Rogaland county, Norway. The rock itself is a 5-cubic-metre (180 cu ft) glacial deposit wedged in a large crevice in the mountain.

title: Kola Superdeep Borehole
fact: The Kola Superdeep Borehole SG-3 is the deepest human-made hole on Earth (since 1979), which attained maximum true vertical depth of 12,262 metres (40,230 ft) in 1989.

title: Lake Baikal
fact: Lake Baikal is a rift lake and the deepest lake in the world. It is situated in southern Siberia, Russia, between the federal subjects of Irkutsk Oblast to the northwest and the Republic of Buryatia to the southeast.

title: Lake Hillier
fact: Lake Hillier is a saline lake on the edge of Middle Island, the largest of the islands and islets that make up the Recherche Archipelago in the Goldfields-Esperance region, off the south coast of Western Australia. It is particularly notable for its pink colour.

title: Lake Nyos
fact: Lake Nyos ( NEE-ohs) is a crater lake in the Northwest Region of Cameroon, located about 315 km (196 mi) northwest of Yaoundé, the capital. Nyos is a deep lake high on the flank of an inactive volcano in the Oku volcanic plain along the Cameroon line of volcanic activity.

title: Lake Toba
fact: Lake Toba is a large natural lake in North Sumatra and Indonesia. The lake is the massive caldera of the Toba supervolcano.

title: Lambert Glacier
fact: Lambert Glacier is a major glacier in East Antarctica. At about 96 km (60 mi) wide, over 435 km (270 mi) long, and about 2,500 m (8,200 ft) deep, it is the world's largest glacier.

title: Lhotse
fact: Lhotse is the fourth-highest mountain on Earth, after Mount Everest, K2, and Kangchenjunga. At an elevation of 8,516 metres (27,940 ft) above sea level, the main summit is on the border between the Tibet Autonomous Region of China and the Khumbu region of Nepal.

title: Litke Deep
fact: Litke Deep is a bathymetric feature in the Arctic Ocean. The deepest point is 5,449 m (17,877 ft) below sea level.

title: Mammoth Cave National Park
fact: Mammoth Cave National Park is a national park of the United States in south-central Kentucky. It encompasses portions of Mammoth Cave, the longest known cave system in the world.

title: Manaslu
fact: Manaslu is the eighth-highest mountain in the world at 8,163 metres (26,781 ft) above sea level. It is in the Mansiri Himal, part of the Nepalese Himalayas, in west-central Nepal.

title: Mariana Trench
fact: The Mariana Trench is the deepest oceanic trench on Earth, located in the western Pacific Ocean, about 200 kilometers (124 mi) east of the Mariana Islands. It is crescent-shaped and measures about 2,550 km (1,580 mi) in length and 69 km (43 mi) in width.

title: Matterhorn
fact: The Matterhorn is a mountain of the Alps, straddling the main watershed and border between Switzerland and Italy.

title: Mauna Kea
fact: Mauna Kea is a dormant shield volcano on the island of Hawaiʻi. Its peak is 13,803 feet (4,207.3 meters) above sea level, making it the highest point in Hawaii and the island with the second highest high point, behind New Guinea.

title: Mauna Loa
fact: Mauna Loa is one of five volcanoes that form the Island of Hawaii in the U.S. state of Hawaii in the Pacific Ocean. Mauna Loa is Earth's largest active volcano by both mass and volume.

title: Mawsynram
fact: Mawsynram is a town in the East Khasi Hills district of Meghalaya state in Northeastern India, 69 km (43 mi) from Shillong, the state capital. Mawsynram receives the highest rainfall in India.

title: Millau Viaduct
fact: The Millau Viaduct is a multispan cable-stayed bridge completed in 2004 across the gorge valley of the Tarn near (west of) Millau in the Aveyron department in the Occitanie Region, in Southern France.

title: Milwaukee Deep
fact: Milwaukee Deep, also known as the Milwaukee Depth, is the deepest part of the Puerto Rico Trench, constituting the deepest points in the Atlantic Ocean.

title: Mir mine
fact: The Mir mine, also called the Mirny mine, is an open pit diamond mine located in Mirny, Sakha Republic, in the Siberian region of eastern Russia. It was the Soviet Union's first developed diamond mine, and became its largest after open-pit mining began in 1957.

title: Molloy Deep
fact: The Molloy Deep is a bathymetric feature in the Fram Strait, within the Greenland Sea east of Greenland and about 160 km (100 mi) west of Svalbard. It is the location of the deepest point in the Arctic Ocean.

title: Mont Blanc
fact: Mont Blanc (UK:; US: ) is a mountain in the Alps, rising 4,807.3 m (15,771.9 ft) above sea level, located right at the Franco-Italian border.

title: Mount Cameroon
fact: Mount Cameroon is an active stratovolcano in the Southwest Region of Cameroon next to the city of Buea near the Gulf of Guinea.

title: Mount Elbrus
fact: Mount Elbrus is the highest mountain in Russia and Europe. It is a dormant stratovolcano rising 5,642 m (18,510 ft) above sea level, and is the highest volcano in Eurasia, as well as the tenth-most prominent peak in the world.

title: Mount Erebus
fact: Mount Erebus is the southernmost active volcano on Earth, located on Ross Island in the Ross Dependency in Antarctica.

title: Mount Kilimanjaro
fact: Mount Kilimanjaro is a large dormant volcano in Tanzania. It is the highest mountain in Africa and the highest free-standing mountain above sea level in the world, at 5,895 m (19,341 ft) above sea level and 4,900 m (16,100 ft) above its plateau base.

title: Mount Kosciuszko
fact: Mount Kosciuszko is the highest mountain of mainland Australia, at 2,228 metres (7,310 ft) above sea level.

title: Mount Logan
fact: Mount Logan is the highest mountain in Canada, and the second-highest peak in North America after Denali. The mountain was named after Sir William Edmond Logan, a Canadian geologist and founder of the Geological Survey of Canada (GSC).

title: Mount Mitchell
fact: Mount Mitchell is the highest peak of the Appalachian Mountains and the highest peak in mainland North America east of the Mississippi River.

title: Mount Stanley
fact: Mount Stanley, also known as Mount Ngaliema, is a mountain located in the Rwenzori range. With an elevation of 5,109 m (16,763 ft), it is the highest mountain of both the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda, and the fourth-highest in Africa.

title: Mount Thor
fact: Mount Thor, officially gazetted as Thor Peak, in Nunavut, Canada, is a mountain with an elevation of 1,675 m (5,495 ft) located in Auyuittuq National Park, on Baffin Island.

title: Mount Whitney
fact: Mount Whitney (Paiute: Tumanguya) is a mountain in California's Sierra Nevada range, and is the highest point in the contiguous United States, with an elevation of 14,505 feet (4,421 m). It is located in East–Central California along the border of Inyo and Tulare counties.

title: Nanga Parbat
fact: Nanga Parbat, known in Shina as Diamer, is the ninth-highest mountain on Earth with its summit at 8,126 m (26,660 ft) above sea level.

title: Nazaré Canyon
fact: The Nazaré Canyon is a submarine canyon just off the coast of Nazaré in the Oeste region of Portugal, in the eastern North Atlantic Ocean.

title: Niagara Falls
fact: Niagara Falls is a group of three waterfalls at the southern end of Niagara Gorge, spanning the border between the Canadian province of Ontario and the U.S. state of New York.

title: North Cape (Norway)
fact: The North Cape is a cape on the northern coast of the island of Magerøya in Northern Norway. The cape is in Nordkapp Municipality in Finnmark county, Norway.

title: Ojos del Salado
fact: Nevado Ojos del Salado is a dormant complex volcano in the Andes on the Argentina–Chile border. It is the highest volcano on Earth and the highest peak in Chile.

title: Old Tjikko
fact: Old Tjikko is an approximately 9,568-year-old Norway spruce, located in the Dalarna province in Sweden. Old Tjikko originally gained fame as the "world's oldest tree".

title: Pole of inaccessibility
fact: In geography, a pole of inaccessibility is the farthest (or the most difficult to reach) location in a given landmass, sea, or other topographical feature, starting from a given boundary, relative to a given criterion.

title: Preikestolen
fact: Preikestolen or Prekestolen (English: 'Pulpit Rock' or 'Pulpit') is a tourist attraction in Strand Municipality in Rogaland county, Norway. Preikestolen is a steep cliff which rises 604 metres (1,982 ft) above Lysefjorden.

title: Puerto Rico Trench
fact: The Puerto Rico Trench is located on the boundary between the North Atlantic Ocean and Caribbean Sea, parallel to and north of Puerto Rico, where the oceanic trench reaches the deepest points in the Atlantic Ocean.

title: Puncak Jaya
fact: Puncak Jaya or Carstensz Pyramid on the island of New Guinea, with an elevation of 4,884 m (16,024 ft), is the highest mountain peak of an island on Earth, and the highest peak in Indonesia and within Oceania.

title: Ras Dashen
fact: Ras Dashen is the highest mountain in Ethiopia. Located in the Simien Mountains National Park in the North Gondar Zone of the Amhara Region, it reaches an elevation of 4,550 metres (14,930 ft).

title: Richat Structure
fact: The Richat Structure, or Guelb er Richât, often called the Eye of Africa is a prominent circular geological feature at the northwestern edge of the Taoudeni Basin, on the Adrar Plateau of the Sahara. It is located near Ouadane in the Adrar Region of Mauritania.

title: Ross Ice Shelf
fact: The Ross Ice Shelf is the largest ice shelf of Antarctica. It is several hundred metres thick. The nearly vertical ice front to the open sea is more than 600 km (370 mi) long, and between 15 and 50 m (50 and 160 ft) high above the water surface.

title: Sunda Trench
fact: The Sunda Trench, earlier known as and sometimes still indicated as the Java Trench, is an oceanic trench located in the Indian Ocean near Sumatra, formed where the Australian-Capricorn plates subduct under a part of the Eurasian plate.

title: Tamu Massif
fact: Tamu Massif is a seamount in the northwest Pacific Ocean, sitting atop a triple junction of mid-ocean ridges. Tamu Massif is located in the Shatsky Rise about 1,600 km (990 mi) east of Japan. The massif covers an area of about 553,000 square kilometres (214,000 mi2).

title: Three Gorges Dam
fact: The Three Gorges Dam, officially known as Yangtze River Three Gorges Water Conservancy Project is a hydroelectric gravity dam that spans the Yangtze River near Sandouping in Yiling District, Yichang, Hubei province, central China, downstream of the Three Gorges.

title: Tonga Trench
fact: The Tonga Trench is an oceanic trench located in the southwestern Pacific Ocean. It is the deepest trench in the Southern hemisphere and the second deepest on Earth after the Mariana Trench.

title: Toubkal
fact: Toubkal, also Jbel Toubkal or Jebel Toubkal, is a mountain in central Morocco, located in the Toubkal National Park. At 4,167 m (13,671 ft), it is the highest peak in Morocco, the Atlas Mountains, North Africa and the Arab world.

title: Trolltunga
fact: Trolltunga is a rock formation situated at an elevaton of 1,126 metres (3,694 ft) above sea level in Ullensvang Municipality in Vestland county, Norway.

title: Ulm Minster
fact: Ulm Minster is a Gothic church of the Evangelical Church in Germany located in Ulm, Baden-Württemberg. It is the second-tallest church building in the world, with a steeple measuring 161.53 metres (530.0 ft).

title: Vatnajökull
fact: Vatnajökull is the largest and most voluminous ice cap in Iceland, and the second largest in area in Europe after the Severny Island ice cap of Novaya Zemlya. It is in the south-east of the island, covering approximately 8% of the country.

title: Veryovkina Cave
fact: Veryovkina Cave is a cave in Abkhazia, Georgia. With a known depth of 2,209 meters (7,247 ft) as of 2025, it is the second deepest-known cave on Earth after Krubera Cave.

title: Victoria Falls
fact: Victoria Falls is a waterfall on the Zambezi River, located on the border between Zambia and Zimbabwe. It is one of the world's largest waterfalls, with a width of 1,708 m (5,604 ft). The region around it has a high degree of biodiversity in both plants and animals.

title: Vinson Massif
fact: Vinson Massif is a large mountain massif in Antarctica that is 21 km (13 mi) long and 13 km (8 mi) wide and lies within the Sentinel Range of the Ellsworth Mountains. It overlooks the Ronne Ice Shelf near the base of the Antarctic Peninsula.

title: Vostok Station
fact: Vostok Station is a Russian research station in inland Princess Elizabeth Land, Antarctica.

title: Yarlung Tsangpo Grand Canyon
fact: The Yarlung Tsangpo Grand Canyon, also known as the Yarlung Zangbo Grand Canyon, the Tsangpo Canyon, the Brahmaputra Canyon or the Tsangpo Gorge, is a canyon along the Yarlung Tsangpo River in Tibet Autonomous Region, China.

title: Yellowstone Caldera
fact: The Yellowstone Caldera, also known as the Yellowstone Plateau Volcanic Field, is a Quaternary volcanic field, caldera complex, and volcanic plateau spanning parts of Wyoming, Idaho, and Montana.
